	  in the crater (under CRATER)   thrown when the Force beats its Hold, as any piece is; one
	                                 that holds is sunk into the part and tipped toward the hit
	  on the rim (under RIM)         never thrown: heaved a little out of the part, its inner
	                                 edge the higher one
	  beyond                         never thrown: moved by a hair, which is what makes the
	                                 crack between two pieces show
	No two pieces are moved alike: each rolls its own share of the sink, the tip and a twist.

	Crack.share(piece) -> number         that distance over the reach
	Crack.holds(piece) -> boolean        true outside the crater: no Force throws the piece
	Crack.pose(piece, random, from) -> CFrame
	                                     where the piece stands once struck (random gives 0 to 1),
	                                     moved on from `from`: where an earlier crack left it,
	                                     its rest when nil. Outside the crater it is lifted and
	                                     turned on from there. In the crater it lies as it fell:
	                                     tipped afresh, sunk as deep as one crack sinks it and
	                                     deeper by what it had sunk before. Never through its
	                                     crust, never out of it, never tilted past MOST_TILT.
	Crack.strike(play, index)            a crust piece a Force has reached and not thrown: queued.
	                                     Not one along the side of a ground's patch (atEdge) beyond
	                                     the rim: moved by a hair it would draw the patch's outline
	Crack.settle(play, count) -> count   gives the queued pieces their stand-ins, within the
	                                     frame's wake budget, and adds their poses to the play's
	                                     move lists after the `count` poses already there
	Crack.returning(play, progress, count) -> count
	                                     the poses of the cracked pieces on their way back to
	                                     rest (Reactor/After's Return), added the same way

	A cracked piece stays RESTING: it stands, only not quite where it stood. play.cracked[index]
	is true from the moment it is queued, play.crackFrame[index] is its pose once it has one;
	a piece thrown later starts from that pose.
]]

local RESTING = 0

local CRATER = 0.42
local RIM = 0.71
-- How far the piece at the hit sinks, as a share of the crust's thickness: its top stays
-- above the base it stands on.
local DEPTH_SHARE = 0.7
-- The least of that depth a crater piece sinks, at the crater's edge.
local EDGE_SINK = 0.19
-- Degrees a crater piece is tipped toward the hit, at the crater's edge and at the hit.
local EDGE_TIP = 8
local HIT_TIP = 24
local CRATER_TWIST = 26
-- The rim: how far out of the part it is heaved (share of the depth), and its tip and twist.
local RIM_LIFT = 0.17
local RIM_TIP = 9
local RIM_TWIST = 9
-- Beyond the rim: a hair.
local HAIR_LIFT = 0.027
local HAIR_TIP = 1.2
-- With every crack it has taken, a piece is at most this share of its crust under its rest
-- or over it.
local MOST_SINK = 0.95
local MOST_LIFT = 0.6
-- And its struck face leans at most this many degrees from how it rests. One crack alone
-- stays under it (36 degrees of tip with 13 of twist lean a face by 38).
local MOST_TILT = 40
local TINY = 1e-4

local Crack = {}

-- Degrees between two unit vectors.
local function between(first, second)
	return math.deg(math.acos(math.clamp(first:Dot(second), -1, 1)))
end

-- The piece's place over the struck face, seen from the hit: its distance as a share of the
-- reach, and the unit direction out from the hit along the face.
local function fromHit(piece)
	local strike = piece.strike
	local normal = strike.normal
	local offset = piece.rest.Position - strike.origin
	local flat = offset - normal * offset:Dot(normal)
	local distance = flat.Magnitude
	if distance > TINY then
		return distance / strike.reach, flat / distance
	end
	-- Right at the hit there is no way out: any direction along the face serves.
	local along = normal:Cross(Vector3.new(1, 0, 0))
	if along.Magnitude < TINY then
		along = normal:Cross(Vector3.new(0, 0, 1))
	end
	return 0, along.Unit
end

function Crack.share(piece)
	local share = fromHit(piece)
	return share
end

function Crack.holds(piece)
	return piece.strike ~= nil and Crack.share(piece) >= CRATER
end

function Crack.pose(piece, random, from)
	local strike = piece.strike
	local normal = strike.normal
	local share, outward = fromHit(piece)
	local depth = strike.crust * DEPTH_SHARE
	local lift, tip, twist
	if share < CRATER then
		local near = 1 - share / CRATER
		lift = -depth * (EDGE_SINK + (1 - EDGE_SINK) * near ^ 1.3) * (0.7 + 0.6 * random())
		tip = (EDGE_TIP + (HIT_TIP - EDGE_TIP) * near) * (0.5 + random())
		twist = (random() - 0.5) * CRATER_TWIST
	elseif share < RIM then
		local rim = 1 - (share - CRATER) / (RIM - CRATER)
		lift = depth * RIM_LIFT * rim * (0.5 + random())
		tip = -RIM_TIP * rim * (0.4 + random())
		twist = (random() - 0.5) * RIM_TWIST * rim
	else
		lift = depth * HAIR_LIFT * (random() - 0.5)
		tip = (random() - 0.5) * HAIR_TIP
		twist = 0
	end
	-- About this axis a positive turn raises the piece's outer edge and lowers its inner one.
	local axis = outward:Cross(normal)
	local turn = CFrame.fromAxisAngle(axis, math.rad(tip)) * CFrame.fromAxisAngle(outward, math.rad(twist))
	local rest = from or piece.rest
	local moved = (rest.Position - piece.rest.Position):Dot(normal)
	local facing = rest.Rotation
	if share < CRATER then
		-- A piece cut out of a tipped one is handed its place in it, which may lie over the face.
		facing = piece.rest.Rotation
		lift += math.min(moved, 0) - moved
	end
	lift = math.clamp(lift, -strike.crust * MOST_SINK - moved, strike.crust * MOST_LIFT - moved)
	-- Of a turn that would lean the piece too far, only the share that stays within is given.
	local turned = turn * facing
	local faceOut = piece.rest:VectorToObjectSpace(normal)
	local leans = between(facing:VectorToWorldSpace(faceOut), normal)
	local wouldLean = between(turned:VectorToWorldSpace(faceOut), normal)
	if wouldLean > MOST_TILT and wouldLean > leans then
		local share = math.clamp((MOST_TILT - leans) / (wouldLean - leans), 0, 1)
		turned = facing:Lerp(turned, share)
	end
	return CFrame.new(rest.Position + normal * lift) * turned
end

function Crack.strike(play, index)
	if play.cracked[index] or play.state[index] ~= RESTING or play.pendingPush[index] then
		return
	end
	-- Along its patch's side and beyond the rim a piece stays at rest (Reactor/Pieces.ofSet).
	local piece = play.pieces[index]
	if piece.atEdge and Crack.share(piece) >= RIM then
		return
	end
	play.cracked[index] = true
	table.insert(play.pendingCrack, index)
end

function Crack.settle(play, count)
	local pending = play.pendingCrack
	if #pending == 0 then
		return count
	end
	local budget = play.settings.wakeBudget
	local taken = 0
	local made = 0
	while taken < #pending and made < budget do
		taken += 1
		local index = pending[taken]
		-- One thrown since it was queued flies from where it stood.
		if play.state[index] == RESTING and not play.pendingPush[index] then
			made += play.display.wake(index) or 1
			play.hidden += 1
			local frame = Crack.pose(play.pieces[index], play.settings.random, play.crackFrame[index])
			play.crackFrame[index] = frame
			count += 1
			play.moveIndices[count] = index
			play.moveFrames[count] = frame
		end
	end
	local remaining = {}
	for position = taken + 1, #pending do
		table.insert(remaining, pending[position])
	end
	play.pendingCrack = remaining
	return count
end

function Crack.returning(play, progress, count)
	for index, frame in pairs(play.crackFrame) do
		if play.state[index] == RESTING then
			count += 1
			play.moveIndices[count] = index
			play.moveFrames[count] = frame:Lerp(play.pieces[index].rest, progress)
		end
	end
	return count
end

return Crack

--[[
	Dice  -  a box as a grid of blocks: what a part of a Reactor breaks into with Break =
	"Blocks". Numbers only, no instances.

	Dice.grid(size, pieces) -> countX, countY, countZ
	    how many blocks along each axis: the grid whose blocks are nearest to cubes and whose
	    number is nearest to `pieces`. A count can rarely be met exactly (50 in a cube is
	    3 x 4 x 4 = 48). An axis too short for a cube of its own is not cut, and the others are
	    cut the finer for it. Never more than Dice.MAX_BLOCKS.
	Dice.cut(size, pieces, random) -> { { offset = Vector3, size = Vector3 }, ... }
	    that grid as blocks that fill the box exactly, for a part that is a plain box. Each
	    axis is cut by planes that run through the whole box, spaced evenly and then shifted a
	    little, so the blocks are an uneven grid: every block touches its neighbours face to
	    face and nothing overlaps or is left out. offset is a block's centre in the box's own
	    space. random gives 0 to 1; the same sequence gives the same blocks.
	Dice.centres(size, pieces) -> { Vector3 }
	    the middles of that grid's cells, evenly spaced: the points the engine cuts a part that
	    is NOT a plain box around (Reactor/Shards). Each fragment is the part of the shape nearest
	    its point, which for an even grid is a cube.
]]

local Dice = {}

-- A part is never cut into more blocks than this.
Dice.MAX_BLOCKS = 240
-- How far a cut may be shifted from its even place, as a share of a block's length.
local SHIFT = 0.22
-- An axis shorter than this share of a cube's edge is not cut.
local UNCUT_UNDER = 0.75
-- grid: how much a block's being off a cube weighs against the count's being off `pieces`.
local SHAPE_WEIGHT = 0.25

local AXES = { "X", "Y", "Z" }

-- The cut planes along one axis of `length`, from -length / 2 to length / 2, both ends included.
local function planes(length, count, random)
	local edges = table.create(count + 1)
	local step = length / count
	edges[1] = -length / 2
	for cut = 1, count - 1 do
		edges[cut + 1] = -length / 2 + step * (cut + (random() * 2 - 1) * SHIFT)
	end
	edges[count + 1] = length / 2
	return edges
end

-- The edge of a cube when `pieces` of them fill the box, and which axes are cut at all: an axis
-- too short for such a cube is left whole and the cube worked out again over the others.
local function cubeEdge(size, pieces)
	local cut = { X = true, Y = true, Z = true }
	local edge = 0
	for _ = 1, #AXES do
		local measure = 1
		local axes = 0
		for _, axis in ipairs(AXES) do
			if cut[axis] then
				measure *= size[axis]
				axes += 1
			end
		end
		if axes == 0 then
			break
		end
		edge = (measure / pieces) ^ (1 / axes)
		local dropped = false
		for _, axis in ipairs(AXES) do
			if cut[axis] and size[axis] < edge * UNCUT_UNDER then
				cut[axis] = false
				dropped = true
			end
		end
		if not dropped then
			break
		end
	end
	return edge, cut
end

-- The counts worth trying along one axis: the nearest to a cube, one fewer and one more.
local function choices(length, edge, isCut)
	if not isCut then
		return { 1 }
	end
	local nearest = math.max(math.round(length / edge), 1)
	local list = {}
	for count = math.max(nearest - 1, 1), nearest + 1 do
		table.insert(list, count)
	end
	return list
end

function Dice.grid(size, pieces)
	pieces = math.clamp(math.floor(pieces), 1, Dice.MAX_BLOCKS)
	local edge, cut = cubeEdge(size, pieces)
	local bestX, bestY, bestZ = 1, 1, 1
	local bestScore = math.huge
	for _, countX in ipairs(choices(size.X, edge, cut.X)) do
		for _, countY in ipairs(choices(size.Y, edge, cut.Y)) do
			for _, countZ in ipairs(choices(size.Z, edge, cut.Z)) do
				local total = countX * countY * countZ
				if total <= Dice.MAX_BLOCKS then
					-- How far the longest edge of a block is from its shortest, over the cut axes.
					local longest, shortest = 0, math.huge
					local counts = { X = countX, Y = countY, Z = countZ }
					for _, axis in ipairs(AXES) do
						if cut[axis] then
							local length = size[axis] / counts[axis]
							longest = math.max(longest, length)
							shortest = math.min(shortest, length)
						end
					end
					local offCube = 0
					if longest > 0 then
						offCube = longest / shortest - 1
					end
					local score = math.abs(total - pieces) / pieces + SHAPE_WEIGHT * offCube
					if score < bestScore then
						bestX, bestY, bestZ = countX, countY, countZ
						bestScore = score
					end
				end
			end
		end
	end
	return bestX, bestY, bestZ
end

function Dice.cut(size, pieces, random)
	local countX, countY, countZ = Dice.grid(size, pieces)
	local edgesX = planes(size.X, countX, random)
	local edgesY = planes(size.Y, countY, random)
	local edgesZ = planes(size.Z, countZ, random)
	local blocks = table.create(countX * countY * countZ)
	for x = 1, countX do
		for y = 1, countY do
			for z = 1, countZ do
				table.insert(blocks, {
					offset = Vector3.new((edgesX[x] + edgesX[x + 1]) / 2, (edgesY[y] + edgesY[y + 1]) / 2, (edgesZ[z] + edgesZ[z + 1]) / 2),
					size = Vector3.new(edgesX[x + 1] - edgesX[x], edgesY[y + 1] - edgesY[y], edgesZ[z + 1] - edgesZ[z]),
				})
			end
		end
	end
	return blocks
end

function Dice.centres(size, pieces)
	local countX, countY, countZ = Dice.grid(size, pieces)
	local centres = table.create(countX * countY * countZ)
	for x = 1, countX do
		for y = 1, countY do
			for z = 1, countZ do
				table.insert(centres, Vector3.new(
					((x - 0.5) / countX - 0.5) * size.X,
					((y - 0.5) / countY - 0.5) * size.Y,
					((z - 0.5) / countZ - 0.5) * size.Z
				))
			end
		end
	end
	return centres
end

return Dice

--[[
	Display  -  what a Reactor's play looks like in the world: a stand-in for every piece that is
	out of place, and the original hidden while its stand-in exists. The four functions Reactor/Play
	calls (wake, move, drop, restore).

	A piece that is a block cut from a part (Reactor/Pieces, Break = "Blocks") gets a stand-in the
	size of the block, and the first block of a part to wake brings stand-ins for all its
	siblings with it: the part is hidden as a whole, so the blocks left standing must be shown.
	A piece that is a shard (Break = "Shards") gets a copy of its template (Reactor/Shards) in
	the part's look of that moment. A shard's template does not sit at the centre of the shard's
	box, which is what a piece's frame is: a shard's stand-in is placed at frame * standOffset.
	The base under cracked ground (piece.fixed) is drawn darker than the part, as broken ground
	is under its surface. A part cut as cracked ground stays solid while it is hidden, on a
	server too: its base never moves, and what is thrown from it lands on it.

	Only stand-ins ever move. They are copies that are not saved (Archivable off, under the
	runtime's folder, marked _PartIcleEmit so the start-up and shut-down sweeps remove strays).
	An original is LIVE user content and is written in one way only: hidden through
	LocalTransparencyModifier, which Roblox neither saves nor replicates, so a crash or a save
	in the middle of a play leaves the place as it was. A server has no such property to use:
	there the original's Transparency, CanCollide and CanQuery are set and put back from a copy
	of their values kept by this display.

	Display.hide(part, onServer, staysSolid) -> kept, Display.show(part, onServer, kept): that
	one write and its undo, for whoever hides an original itself. A ground with open cracks is
	hidden once by Reactor/GroundDisplay, however many cracks are open, so the displays of its
	cracks are made with keepOriginals and leave it alone.
	display.clear() removes every stand-in and shows what this display hid.
]]

local EngineAttr = require(script.Parent.Parent.EngineAttr)
local Index = require(script.Parent.Index)

local CONFIG_NAME = "PartIcleProperties"
-- How bright the base under cracked ground is, against the part's own colour.
local BASE_SHADE = 0.6

local Display = {}

-- Whether a stand-in takes a child of its original along: what draws on the part does. Parts
-- and anything that holds parts do not (they are pieces of their own, as Modules/Scatter's
-- field under a one-part Reactor), nor joints, values, code or the plugin's own children.
function Display.travels(child)
	if child:IsA("BasePart") or child:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("BasePart", true) then
		return false
	end
	if child:IsA("JointInstance") or child:IsA("Constraint") or child:IsA("WeldConstraint") or child:IsA("NoCollisionConstraint") then
		return false
	end
	if child:IsA("LuaSourceContainer") or child:IsA("ValueBase") then
		return false
	end
	if child.Name == CONFIG_NAME or child:GetAttribute("Transformed") then
		return false
	end
	return true
end

-- Whether a piece is of a part cut as cracked ground: its crust (strike) or its base (fixed).
function Display.cracked(piece)
	return piece.strike ~= nil or piece.fixed == true
end

-- A piece of a ground's patch (Reactor/Wounds) carries the ground's own Textures, so a patch
-- at rest cannot be told from the ground around it. Measured in Studio: a Texture on a
-- fragment is laid from the +X and +Z edges of the fragment's own extents box, which is the
-- piece's box. Only the top face is measured: a ground cracked on another face carries none.
local function carryTextures(copy, piece)
	local cut = piece.cut
	if not cut or piece.fixed or cut.face.axis ~= "Y" or cut.face.side ~= 1 then
		return
	end
	local part = piece.part
	local centre = part.CFrame:PointToObjectSpace(piece.rest.Position)
	for _, child in ipairs(part:GetChildren()) do
		if child:IsA("Texture") and child.Face == Enum.NormalId.Top then
			local texture = child:Clone()
			texture.OffsetStudsU = child.OffsetStudsU + part.Size.X / 2 - (centre.X + piece.halfExt.X)
			texture.OffsetStudsV = child.OffsetStudsV + part.Size.Z / 2 - (centre.Z + piece.halfExt.Z)
			-- The ground's own Texture is hidden while a wound is open: the copy is not.
			EngineAttr.writeProp(texture, "LocalTransparencyModifier", 0)
			texture.Parent = copy
		end
	end
end

-- A shard's stand-in: a copy of its template, looking as the part does now.
local function makeShard(piece)
	local part = piece.part
	local copy = piece.shard:Clone()
	copy.Color = part.Color
	if piece.fixed then
		copy.Color = Color3.new(part.Color.R * BASE_SHADE, part.Color.G * BASE_SHADE, part.Color.B * BASE_SHADE)
	end
	copy.Material = part.Material
	copy.MaterialVariant = part.MaterialVariant
	copy.Transparency = part.Transparency
	copy.Reflectance = part.Reflectance
	copy.Archivable = false
	copy.Anchored = true
	copy.CanCollide = false
	copy.CanQuery = false
	copy.CanTouch = false
	copy.Locked = true
	copy:SetAttribute("_PartIcleEmit", true)
	carryTextures(copy, piece)
	return copy
end

local function makeStandIn(piece)
	if piece.shard then
		return makeShard(piece)
	end
	local part = piece.part
	local copy = Instance.fromExisting(part)
	copy.Archivable = false
	copy.Anchored = true
	copy.CanCollide = false
	copy.CanQuery = false
	copy.CanTouch = false
	copy.Locked = true
	-- A Reactor that is one part would hand its own marks to its stand-in.
	Index.unmark(copy)
	copy:SetAttribute("_PartIcleEmit", true)
	if piece.blockSize then
		-- A block carries nothing over: what sat on the whole part's faces has no place on a cut of it.
		copy.Size = piece.blockSize
		return copy
	end
	for _, child in ipairs(part:GetChildren()) do
		if Display.travels(child) then
			local childCopy = child:Clone()
			if childCopy then
				childCopy.Parent = copy
			end
		end
	end
	return copy
end

-- Hides or shows a LIVE original and the Decals and Textures directly on it.
local function setLocalHidden(part, hidden)
	local modifier = 0
	if hidden then
		modifier = 1
	end
	EngineAttr.writeProp(part, "LocalTransparencyModifier", modifier)
	for _, child in ipairs(part:GetChildren()) do
		if child:IsA("Decal") then
			EngineAttr.writeProp(child, "LocalTransparencyModifier", modifier)
		end
	end
end

-- Hides a LIVE original and returns what Display.show needs to put it back. staysSolid:
-- cracked ground, which goes on carrying what stands and lands on it.
function Display.hide(part, onServer, staysSolid)
	if not onServer then
		setLocalHidden(part, true)
		return true
	end
	local kept = { Transparency = part.Transparency, CanCollide = part.CanCollide, CanQuery = part.CanQuery }
	EngineAttr.writeProp(part, "Transparency", 1)
	if staysSolid then
		return kept
	end
	EngineAttr.writeProp(part, "CanCollide", false)
	EngineAttr.writeProp(part, "CanQuery", false)
	return kept
end

-- Shows a LIVE original that Display.hide hid; `kept` is what hide returned.
function Display.show(part, onServer, kept)
	if not part.Parent then
		return
	end
	if not onServer then
		setLocalHidden(part, false)
		return
	end
	EngineAttr.writeProp(part, "Transparency", kept.Transparency)
	EngineAttr.writeProp(part, "CanCollide", kept.CanCollide)
	EngineAttr.writeProp(part, "CanQuery", kept.CanQuery)
end

-- Shows a LIVE part that is found hidden with no play to answer for it (Reactor/init:
-- ShowStrandedReactors). Only the local hide can be undone this way: a server's hide keeps the
-- values to put back in its display, and they went with it.
function Display.unhide(part)
	setLocalHidden(part, false)
end

-- pieces: Reactor/Pieces records. folder: where stand-ins live. onServer: true where there is
-- no local hide and the original's own properties are used. keepOriginals: the originals are
-- somebody else's to hide and show.
function Display.new(pieces, folder, onServer, keepOriginals)
	local standIns = {}
	-- part -> true while it is hidden, or (on a server) the values to put back.
	local hidden = {}
	local moveParts = {}
	local moveCount = 0
	local display = {}
	-- Only a display with shards rewrites the frames it is handed.
	local offsetFrames = nil
	for _, piece in ipairs(pieces) do
		if piece.standOffset then
			offsetFrames = {}
			break
		end
	end

	-- Hides a LIVE original once, however many of its blocks ask.
	local function hideOriginal(part, staysSolid)
		if keepOriginals or hidden[part] then
			return
		end
		hidden[part] = Display.hide(part, onServer, staysSolid)
	end

	local function showOriginal(part)
		local kept = hidden[part]
		if not kept then
			return
		end
		hidden[part] = nil
		Display.show(part, onServer, kept)
	end

	local function place(index)
		local piece = pieces[index]
		local copy = makeStandIn(piece)
		if piece.standOffset then
			copy.CFrame = piece.rest * piece.standOffset
		else
			copy.CFrame = piece.rest
		end
		copy.Parent = folder
		standIns[index] = copy
	end

	-- Returns how many stand-ins it made, which is what a frame's wake budget counts.
	function display.wake(index)
		local piece = pieces[index]
		local made = 0
		if piece.siblings then
			for _, sibling in ipairs(piece.siblings) do
				if not standIns[sibling] then
					place(sibling)
					made += 1
				end
			end
		elseif not standIns[index] then
			place(index)
			made = 1
		end
		hideOriginal(piece.part, Display.cracked(piece))
		return made
	end

	-- Every index must have its stand-in: BulkMoveTo takes a missing one as the end of the list
	-- and refuses the move. Reactor/Play drops a lost piece before it lists the frame's moves.
	function display.move(indices, frames, count)
		for position = 1, count do
			moveParts[position] = standIns[indices[position]]
		end
		for position = count + 1, moveCount do
			moveParts[position] = nil
		end
		if offsetFrames then
			for position = 1, count do
				local standOffset = pieces[indices[position]].standOffset
				if standOffset then
					offsetFrames[position] = frames[position] * standOffset
				else
					offsetFrames[position] = frames[position]
				end
			end
			for position = count + 1, moveCount do
				offsetFrames[position] = nil
			end
			frames = offsetFrames
		end
		moveCount = count
		workspace:BulkMoveTo(moveParts, frames, Enum.BulkMoveMode.FireCFrameChanged)
	end

	function display.drop(index)
		local copy = standIns[index]
		if copy then
			copy:Destroy()
			standIns[index] = nil
		end
	end

	-- A block takes its siblings with it: the part comes back whole or not at all.
	function display.restore(index)
		local piece = pieces[index]
		if piece.siblings then
			for _, sibling in ipairs(piece.siblings) do
				display.drop(sibling)
			end
		else
			display.drop(index)
		end
		showOriginal(piece.part)
	end

	function display.clear()
		for index, copy in pairs(standIns) do
			copy:Destroy()
			standIns[index] = nil
		end
		for part in pairs(table.clone(hidden)) do
			showOriginal(part)
		end
	end

	-- The original of a piece, for whoever must leave it out of a ray.
	function display.original(index)
		return pieces[index].part
	end

	return display
end

return Display

--[[
	Driven  -  the pieces of a play that a Continuous Force is carrying (wind, a tornado, a pull).
	Part of Reactor/Play, split out for size: it reads and writes the play's own tables.

	A Continuous Force is a flow: its Strength is the speed, in studs per second, it carries a
	piece at, along the direction Force/Fields gives. A carried piece takes up that speed within
	a fraction of a second (GRIP). Gravity still holds it down unless the flow rises: a wind along
	the ground rolls pieces over it, while a rising flow carries a piece up at the flow's own
	speed, slower where the Force has faded, until the piece leaves the shape and falls.
	Each piece is stepped live, one floor ray and one wall ray a step, only while a Force holds
	it; when none does it is put back on a built path (Play:_launch) and lands like any other.

	A carried piece's way is kept (play.track[index] = { frames, times }: a pose every
	TRACK_EVERY seconds from the moment a Force took hold of it, thinned when it grows long),
	so that Reactor/After's Return can take it back the way it came, round the tornado and
	all. A piece a Force let go and takes up again out of the same flight keeps one way, the
	flight between included. Play:_launch drops the way of a piece that is launched from
	anywhere but where a Force let it go: a Return would jump from one to the other.

	capture(play, record) takes in the pieces a Continuous record has reached.
	poseAt(track, seconds) -> the pose `seconds` after the Force took hold.
	step(play, dt, count) advances every driven piece and adds its pose to the play's move lists
	from position count + 1; returns the new count.
]]

local Fields = require(script.Parent.Parent.Force.Fields)
local Trajectory = require(script.Parent.Parent.Rocks.Trajectory)

local RESTING = 0
local FLYING = 1
local LANDED = 2
local GONE = 3
local DRIVEN = 4

local ZERO = Vector3.new(0, 0, 0)
local TINY = 1e-4
-- A carried piece's way: a pose this often, and at most this many before every other goes.
local TRACK_EVERY = 0.05
local TRACK_MOST = 160
-- Steps of at most this long, and no more than a few a frame.
local STEP_SECONDS = 1 / 60
local MAX_STEPS = 3
-- How fast a piece takes up the Force's speed, per second.
local GRIP = 6
-- How far below a piece the floor ray looks beyond the piece's own half height.
local FLOOR_MARGIN = 0.1
-- A flow whose upward part is at least this share of its speed spares a piece gravity
-- altogether; a level flow spares none.
local LIFTING_SHARE = 0.25
-- Turbulence: how fast the gusts change, and how far apart two pieces' gusts are.
local GUST_RATE = 1.7
local GUST_SPREAD = 0.37

local Driven = {}

Driven.STATE = DRIVEN

-- How far a turned box reaches along a unit direction.
local function support(rotation, halfExt, direction)
	return math.abs(rotation.XVector:Dot(direction)) * halfExt.X
		+ math.abs(rotation.YVector:Dot(direction)) * halfExt.Y
		+ math.abs(rotation.ZVector:Dot(direction)) * halfExt.Z
end

-- What the Continuous Forces of a play ask of a piece at `position`: the velocity to carry it
-- at, the share of gravity it is spared (0 for a level flow, 1 for one that rises), and whether
-- any Force holds it at all.
local function flowAt(play, index, position)
	local piece = play.pieces[index]
	local velocity = ZERO
	local held = false
	for record in pairs(play.kicks) do
		if record.actsAs == "Continuous" and not record.ended then
			local strength = record.strength
			local direction, distance, distance01 = Fields.sample(record.field, position, strength < 0)
			if direction and distance <= record.front then
				local share = Fields.kept(record.falloff, distance01) * Fields.sizeShare(piece.size, record.sizeResponse)
				local gust = 1
				if record.turbulence > 0 then
					gust = 1 + record.turbulence * 2 * math.noise(play.clock * GUST_RATE, index * GUST_SPREAD, record.seed * 10)
				end
				velocity += direction * (math.abs(strength) * share * gust)
				held = true
			end
		end
	end
	local speed = velocity.Magnitude
	local rising = 0
	if speed > TINY then
		rising = math.clamp(velocity.Y / (speed * LIFTING_SHARE), 0, 1)
	end
	return velocity, rising, held
end

-- Takes a piece that is out of place off its path and into the flow, from where it is.
-- Adds a pose to a way, `seconds` after its start. One that has grown long keeps every other.
local function note(track, seconds, frame)
	table.insert(track.frames, frame)
	table.insert(track.times, seconds)
	track.due = seconds + track.every
	if #track.frames <= TRACK_MOST then
		return
	end
	local frames, times = {}, {}
	for place = 1, #track.frames, 2 do
		table.insert(frames, track.frames[place])
		table.insert(times, track.times[place])
	end
	if times[#times] ~= seconds then
		table.insert(frames, frame)
		table.insert(times, seconds)
	end
	track.frames = frames
	track.times = times
	track.every *= 2
end

function Driven.poseAt(track, seconds)
	local frames, times = track.frames, track.times
	local last = #times
	if seconds <= times[1] then
		return frames[1]
	elseif seconds >= times[last] then
		return frames[last]
	end
	local low, high = 1, last
	while high - low > 1 do
		local middle = (low + high) // 2
		if times[middle] <= seconds then
			low = middle
		else
			high = middle
		end
	end
	return frames[low]:Lerp(frames[high], (seconds - times[low]) / (times[high] - times[low]))
end

-- The way of a piece a Force takes hold of at `frame`. Out of the flight the last Force let
-- it go into, it carries on with the way it has, the flight so far added to it.
local function wayFrom(play, index, frame, elapsed)
	local track = play.track[index]
	if not track or track.releasedAt ~= play.pathStart[index] then
		play.track[index] = { frames = { frame }, times = { 0 }, every = TRACK_EVERY, due = TRACK_EVERY, started = play.clock }
		return
	end
	local released = track.releasedAt - track.started
	local flown = track.every
	while flown < elapsed do
		note(track, released + flown, Trajectory.evaluate(play.path[index], flown, play.gravity[index]))
		flown += track.every
	end
	note(track, released + elapsed, frame)
	track.releasedAt = nil
end

local function enter(play, index)
	local elapsed = play.clock - play.pathStart[index]
	local gravity = play.gravity[index]
	local frame = Trajectory.evaluate(play.path[index], elapsed, gravity)
	wayFrom(play, index, frame, elapsed)
	local velocity, spin = Trajectory.velocity(play.path[index], elapsed, gravity)
	if spin.Magnitude < TINY then
		spin = play.path[index].segs[1].w
	end
	play.drivePosition[index] = frame.Position
	play.driveRotation[index] = frame.Rotation
	play.driveVelocity[index] = velocity
	play.driveSpin[index] = spin
	play.state[index] = DRIVEN
	table.insert(play.driven, index)
end

-- The pieces a Continuous record has reached: a resting one is woken (it joins the flow on a
-- later frame, once it has its stand-in), one already out of place joins now. A Force that
-- would carry a piece no faster than Hold leaves it be.
function Driven.capture(play, record)
	local strength = record.strength
	local pulls = strength < 0
	for index, piece in ipairs(play.pieces) do
		local state = play.state[index]
		if state ~= DRIVEN and state ~= GONE then
			local direction, distance, distance01 = Fields.sample(record.field, play:_position(index), pulls)
			if direction and distance <= record.front then
				local speed = math.abs(strength) * Fields.kept(record.falloff, distance01) * Fields.sizeShare(piece.size, record.sizeResponse)
				if speed > play:_holdOf(index) then
					if state == RESTING then
						play:_push(index, ZERO)
					elseif state == FLYING or state == LANDED then
						enter(play, index)
					end
					play:_takeTime(record)
				end
			end
		end
	end
end

-- One step of one piece. Returns its new position, velocity and rotation.
local function advance(play, index, position, velocity, rotation, flow, spared, stepSeconds)
	local piece = play.pieces[index]
	local gravity = play.gravity[index]
	velocity += (flow - velocity) * math.min(GRIP * stepSeconds, 1)
	velocity += Vector3.new(0, -gravity * (1 - spared) * stepSeconds, 0)
	local move = velocity * stepSeconds

	-- Walls: what lies ahead along the level part of the move.
	local level = Vector3.new(move.X, 0, move.Z)
	local levelDistance = level.Magnitude
	if levelDistance > TINY then
		local ahead = level / levelDistance
		local wall = play.castRay(position, ahead * (levelDistance + support(rotation, piece.halfExt, ahead)))
		if wall then
			local into = move:Dot(wall.Normal)
			if into < 0 then
				move -= wall.Normal * into
			end
			local speedInto = velocity:Dot(wall.Normal)
			if speedInto < 0 then
				velocity -= wall.Normal * speedInto
			end
		end
	end

	-- Floor: the piece may not sink below its own half height above what is under it.
	local halfHeight = support(rotation, piece.halfExt, Vector3.new(0, 1, 0))
	local floor = play.castRay(position, Vector3.new(0, -(halfHeight + math.max(-move.Y, 0) + FLOOR_MARGIN), 0))
	if floor then
		local lowest = floor.Position.Y + halfHeight
		if position.Y + move.Y < lowest then
			move = Vector3.new(move.X, lowest - position.Y, move.Z)
			if velocity.Y < 0 then
				velocity = Vector3.new(velocity.X, 0, velocity.Z)
			end
		end
	end

	local spin = play.driveSpin[index]
	local turn = spin.Magnitude
	if turn * stepSeconds > TINY then
		rotation = CFrame.fromAxisAngle(spin / turn, turn * stepSeconds) * rotation
	end
	return position + move, velocity, rotation
end

function Driven.step(play, dt, count)
	local driven = play.driven
	if #driven == 0 or dt <= 0 then
		return count
	end
	local steps = math.clamp(math.ceil(dt / STEP_SECONDS), 1, MAX_STEPS)
	local stepSeconds = dt / steps
	local place = 1
	while place <= #driven do
		local index = driven[place]
		local position = play.drivePosition[index]
		local velocity = play.driveVelocity[index]
		local rotation = play.driveRotation[index]
		local held = true
		for _ = 1, steps do
			local flow, spared, inside = flowAt(play, index, position)
			if not inside then
				held = false
				break
			end
			position, velocity, rotation = advance(play, index, position, velocity, rotation, flow, spared, stepSeconds)
		end

		local frame = rotation + position
		play.lastFrame[index] = frame
		local track = play.track[index]
		local carried = play.clock - track.started
		if held then
			if carried >= track.due then
				note(track, carried, frame)
			end
			play.drivePosition[index] = position
			play.driveVelocity[index] = velocity
			play.driveRotation[index] = rotation
			count += 1
			play.moveIndices[count] = index
			play.moveFrames[count] = frame
			place += 1
		else
			-- No Force holds it any more: back onto a built path, from here, at this speed.
			local last = #driven
			driven[place] = driven[last]
			driven[last] = nil
			play.state[index] = LANDED
			-- Its way ends where its flight begins: Play:_launch keeps a way marked so.
			note(track, carried, frame)
			track.kept = true
			track.releasedAt = play.clock
			play:_launch(index, frame, velocity, play.driveSpin[index])
		end
	end
	return count
end

return Driven

--[[
	Entries  -  the entry of a Reactor that is not at rest: its play, its display and its place
	on the engine's list. Part of the Reactor mixin (Reactor/init), split out for size: every
	function takes the Particle table as `self` and reads and writes the two tables init keeps
	on it, _reactorPlays (reactor -> entry) and _reactorCutting (reactor -> cutting state).

	An entry is { reactor, group, play, pData or nil, cracksAgain, pieceCount, cracks, wounds }.
	play is over every part but the grounds: a plain block-shaped part of a Reactor with
	Break = "Shards" and Shard Pattern "Cracks" is never cut whole. Its cracks are wounds
	(Reactor/Wounds, entry.wounds; nil for a Reactor without grounds), each with a play of its
	own, and what is intact of it is drawn by Reactor/GroundDisplay. A Reactor stood up
	somewhere else (an emit at an origin) has no grounds: all of it is in the one play.
	A cutting state is { records, place, emitCtx }: what waits for a Reactor's shards.

	Entries.entryFor(self, reactor, emitCtx, record) -> entry | nil, cutting state
	    The entry of a Reactor, made if it is at rest. nil when it has no pieces or no settings.
	    nil and the cutting state when its shards have to be cut first (Reactor/Shards): the
	    caller leaves with that state what it wanted the entry for. `record` is the Force that
	    asks, if one does.
	Entries.resume(self, entry) -> boolean   puts a play back on the engine's list; false when
	                                         the particle cap refused it
	Entries.putBack(entry)                   the Reactor as built: play restored, wounds closed
	Entries.discard(self, entry)             puts it back and forgets the entry
	Entries.follow(self, entry, record)      a Force a Reactor that is out of place could feel:
	                                         its plays follow it, and an Impulse cracks it
	Entries.step(entry, step, dt, override, frozen) -> "active" | "dormant" | "done"
	    Steps the play by `step` seconds and the wounds by their own time (Reactor/Wounds).
	Entries.crackAgain(self, entry, record, kicked)
	    An Impulse has reached a Reactor that is out of place: cracked ground cracks again where
	    it is (Reactor/Recrack). Nothing for any other Reactor.
	Entries.forget(cutting)                  drops what waits for a Reactor's shards
	Entries.emitOrigin(emitCtx) -> origin, fullPose | nil
	Entries.prepare(self, item)              cuts a Reactor's shards ahead (PrepareReactor)
]]

local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local RangeMod = require(script.Parent.Parent.Range)
local Play = require(script.Parent.Play)
local Pieces = require(script.Parent.Pieces)
local Support = require(script.Parent.Support)
local Display = require(script.Parent.Display)
local Shards = require(script.Parent.Shards)
local Sites = require(script.Parent.Sites)
local Recrack = require(script.Parent.Recrack)
local Wounds = require(script.Parent.Wounds)
local Patches = require(script.Parent.Patches)
local GroundDisplay = require(script.Parent.GroundDisplay)

-- Pieces given a stand-in, and paths built, per Reactor per frame.
local WAKE_BUDGET = 100
local BUILD_BUDGET = 150
-- A piece is carried by the world when something that is not its Reactor lies this close under it.
local ANCHOR_REACH = 0.3
-- No strip of a ground between two wounds, or a wound and its edge, is thinner than this.
local GROUND_SNAP = 2

local Entries = {}

local function playSettings(data, isAnchored)
	return {
		Hold = data.Hold,
		HoldSpread = data.HoldSpread,
		Collapse = data.Collapse,
		isAnchored = isAnchored,
		After = data.After,
		AfterDelay = data.AfterDelay,
		AfterTime = data.AfterTime,
		MaxPieces = data.MaxPieces,
		MaxAirTime = data.MaxAirTime,
		wakeBudget = WAKE_BUDGET,
		buildBudget = BUILD_BUDGET,
		random = math.random,
		rollGravity = function()
			return RangeMod.RandomValueFromRange(data.Gravity)
		end,
		rollBounciness = function()
			return RangeMod.RandomValueFromRange(data.Bounciness)
		end,
		rollFriction = function()
			return RangeMod.RandomValueFromRange(data.Friction)
		end,
		rollTumble = function()
			return math.rad(RangeMod.RandomValueFromRange(data.TumbleSpeed))
		end,
	}
end

-- A Reactor's own frame, which an origin stands in for.
local function hostFrame(reactor)
	if reactor:IsA("Model") then
		return reactor:GetPivot()
	end
	return reactor.CFrame
end

-- Where an emit puts the Reactor: an origin and whether its rotation counts, or nil in place.
function Entries.emitOrigin(emitCtx)
	if not emitCtx then
		return nil
	end
	local origin = nil
	if emitCtx.EventOriginResolver then
		origin = emitCtx.EventOriginResolver()
	end
	origin = origin or emitCtx.EventOriginCF
	if not origin then
		return nil
	end
	return origin, emitCtx.UseFullOrigin == true
end

-- Whether a Reactor's plain blocks are grounds: cracked where they are struck, never cut whole.
local function hasGrounds(data, emitCtx)
	return data.Break == "Shards" and data.ShardPattern == "Cracks" and Entries.emitOrigin(emitCtx) == nil
end

-- A play over some pieces of a Reactor, and its display. Rays skip the runtime's own folders
-- and, piece by piece, the originals that are hidden; the pieces still standing stay solid to
-- the ones in the air. keepOriginals: the pieces are a wound's, whose ground is hidden and
-- shown by Reactor/GroundDisplay.
local function makePlay(self, reactor, data, pieces, keepOriginals)
	local params = RaycastParams.new()
	params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
	params.RespectCanCollide = true
	params.FilterDescendantsInstances = { self:GetFolder(), self:GetPoolFolder() }

	local onServer = RunService:IsServer() and not RunService:IsClient()
	local display = Display.new(pieces, self:GetFolder(), onServer, keepOriginals)
	local showStandIn = display.wake
	local filtered = {}
	display.wake = function(index)
		local made = showStandIn(index)
		local original = display.original(index)
		-- Cracked ground is left in the rays' way: its base stands, and its pieces land on it.
		if not filtered[original] and not Display.cracked(pieces[index]) then
			filtered[original] = true
			params:AddToFilter(original)
		end
		return made
	end
	local function castRay(origin, displacement)
		return workspace:Raycast(origin, displacement, params)
	end

	-- What carries a piece is the world under it, the Reactor itself left out of the ray.
	local worldParams = RaycastParams.new()
	worldParams.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
	worldParams.RespectCanCollide = true
	worldParams.FilterDescendantsInstances = { reactor, self:GetFolder(), self:GetPoolFolder() }
	local function isAnchored(index)
		local piece = pieces[index]
		if piece.fixed then
			return true
		end
		local drop = Support.worldHalf(piece).Y + ANCHOR_REACH
		return workspace:Raycast(piece.rest.Position, Vector3.new(0, -drop, 0), worldParams) ~= nil
	end

	local settings = playSettings(data, isAnchored)
	-- A wound gives its ground back when it is done, after a Fade too (Reactor/After.close).
	settings.closes = keepOriginals == true
	return Play.new(pieces, settings, display, castRay), display
end

-- The wounds of a Reactor's grounds, or nil when it has none.
local function woundsOf(self, entry, reactor, data, grounds)
	if #grounds == 0 then
		return nil
	end
	local onServer = RunService:IsServer() and not RunService:IsClient()
	local groundDisplay = GroundDisplay.new(self:GetFolder(), onServer)
	return Wounds.new({
		grounds = grounds,
		pieceCount = data.Pieces,
		maxPieces = data.MaxPieces,
		after = data.After,
		afterDelay = data.AfterDelay,
		snap = GROUND_SNAP,
		cut = Patches.cut,
		play = function(pieces)
			return makePlay(self, reactor, data, pieces, true)
		end,
		draw = groundDisplay.draw,
		isCurrent = function()
			return self._reactorPlays[reactor] == entry
		end,
		revive = function()
			if not Entries.resume(self, entry) then
				Entries.discard(self, entry)
			end
		end,
	})
end

-- The entry of a Reactor at rest, or nil when it has neither pieces nor grounds. With an
-- emitCtx that carries an origin the stand-ins start at that place, not at the parts.
local function newEntry(self, reactor, data, emitCtx, shardSets)
	local grounds = {}
	local isGround = {}
	if hasGrounds(data, emitCtx) then
		for _, part in ipairs(Pieces.parts(reactor)) do
			if Pieces.isPlainBlock(part) then
				isGround[part] = true
				table.insert(grounds, { part = part, frame = part.CFrame, size = part.Size })
			end
		end
	end
	local pieces = Pieces.collect(reactor, data.Break, data.Pieces, shardSets and function(part)
		return shardSets[part]
	end, function(part)
		return isGround[part] == true
	end)
	if #pieces == 0 and #grounds == 0 then
		return nil
	end
	local origin, fullPose = Entries.emitOrigin(emitCtx)
	if origin then
		Pieces.carry(pieces, hostFrame(reactor), origin, fullPose)
	end

	local entry = {
		reactor = reactor,
		group = data.Group,
		play = makePlay(self, reactor, data, pieces, false),
		pData = nil,
		-- Reactor/Recrack: whether later Impulses crack this ground again, and those that wait to.
		cracksAgain = data.Break == "Shards" and data.ShardPattern == "Cracks",
		pieceCount = data.Pieces,
		cracks = {},
	}
	entry.wounds = woundsOf(self, entry, reactor, data, grounds)
	return entry
end

function Entries.resume(self, entry)
	if entry.pData then
		return true
	end
	local pData = {
		Type = "Reactor",
		VisualPart = nil,
		StartTime = os.clock(),
		TotalKeyFrames = 1,
		CurrentStep = -1,
		LifeTime = math.huge,
		PartLife = 0,
		Graphs = {},
		Seeds = {},
		_effectiveElapsed = 0,
		_sourceItem = entry.reactor,
		_entry = entry,
	}
	pData._onReclaim = function()
		if entry.pData == pData then
			entry.pData = nil
		end
	end
	self._seedTsOverride(pData, entry.reactor)
	entry.pData = pData
	self:_registerEmit(pData, nil)
	return entry.pData == pData
end

function Entries.putBack(entry)
	entry.play:restore()
	if entry.wounds then
		entry.wounds:restore()
	end
end

function Entries.discard(self, entry)
	Entries.putBack(entry)
	self._reactorPlays[entry.reactor] = nil
end

-- `kicked` is the record's list of the pieces it has kicked in the play.
function Entries.crackAgain(self, entry, record, kicked)
	if not entry.cracksAgain or record.actsAs ~= "Impulse" then
		return
	end
	Recrack.request(entry, record, kicked, function()
		return self._reactorPlays[entry.reactor] == entry
	end, function()
		if not Entries.resume(self, entry) then
			Entries.discard(self, entry)
		end
	end)
end

function Entries.follow(self, entry, record)
	local follows = entry.play:watch(record)
	local wounds = entry.wounds
	if wounds then
		-- The grounds crack whatever the other parts' play is doing.
		wounds:strike(record)
		if wounds:watch(record) or wounds:busy() then
			follows = true
		end
	end
	if not follows then
		return
	end
	if not Entries.resume(self, entry) then
		Entries.discard(self, entry)
		return
	end
	Entries.crackAgain(self, entry, record, entry.play.kicks[record])
end

function Entries.step(entry, step, dt, override, frozen)
	local status = entry.play:step(step)
	if not entry.wounds then
		return status
	end
	local woundStatus = entry.wounds:step(dt, override, frozen)
	if status == "active" or woundStatus == "active" then
		return "active"
	end
	if status == "done" and woundStatus == "done" then
		return "done"
	end
	return "dormant"
end

-- Whether a Shard Pattern is cut around a Force, and so only once one has arrived.
local function cutAroundHit(pattern)
	return pattern == "Around hit" or pattern == "Cracks"
end

-- Whether a Reactor's parts are cut by the engine at all, and whether that cut waits for a Force.
local function cutByEngine(data)
	return data.Break == "Shards" or data.Break == "Blocks"
end
local function waitsForHit(data)
	return data.Break == "Shards" and cutAroundHit(data.ShardPattern)
end

-- What the engine cuts each part of a Reactor into, with Break = "Shards" or "Blocks". sets:
-- part -> its kept shards, for the parts that have them (a part without moves whole). jobs: the
-- parts still to be cut. `hit` is where a Force is, for the patterns cut around it; with `reach`
-- as well (that Force's Range) the cut is cracked ground, and a part its rings do not reach
-- moves whole. With Blocks the points are an even grid, and a plain box is left to Reactor/Dice.
-- grounds = true: the Reactor's plain boxes are grounds (hasGrounds), left to Reactor/Wounds.
local function shardPlan(reactor, data, hit, reach, grounds)
	local sets = {}
	local jobs = {}
	local blocks = data.Break == "Blocks"
	for order, part in ipairs(Pieces.parts(reactor)) do
		local count = Sites.count(part.Size, data.Pieces)
		-- A plain box is cut by arithmetic with Blocks, and as a ground is not cut whole at all.
		if (blocks or grounds) and Pieces.isPlainBlock(part) then
			count = 0
		end
		local hitInPart = nil
		if hit then
			hitInPart = part.CFrame:PointToObjectSpace(hit)
			local nearest = Sites.hitIn(part.Size, hitInPart)
			if not reach then
				hitInPart = nearest
			elseif (hitInPart - nearest).Magnitude > reach * Sites.RUN_ON then
				count = 0
			end
		end
		if count >= 2 and Shards.cuttable(part) then
			local seed = order * 7919 + 13
			local key = Shards.key(part, count, seed, hitInPart, reach, blocks)
			local shards = Shards.get(part, key)
			if shards == nil then
				table.insert(jobs, { part = part, key = key, count = count, seed = seed, hit = hitInPart, reach = reach, grid = blocks })
			elseif shards then
				sets[part] = shards
			end
		end
	end
	return sets, jobs
end

-- Has a Reactor's missing shards cut and, when they are kept, gives it the entry it was owed:
-- stood up when an emit asked for that, following the Forces that are still alive and struck
-- once by the Impulses that are over. A restore empties the state (forget, below): the cut
-- goes on and is kept, and nobody is owed an entry any more.
local function startCutting(self, reactor, data, sets, jobs, hit)
	local state = { records = {}, place = false, emitCtx = nil }
	self._reactorCutting[reactor] = state
	Shards.prepare(jobs, function()
		if self._reactorCutting[reactor] ~= state then
			return
		end
		self._reactorCutting[reactor] = nil
		local wanted = state.place or #state.records > 0
		if not wanted or not self.Connection or not reactor.Parent or self._reactorPlays[reactor] then
			return
		end
		for _, job in ipairs(jobs) do
			sets[job.part] = Shards.get(job.part, job.key) or nil
		end
		local entry = newEntry(self, reactor, data, state.emitCtx, sets)
		if not entry then
			return
		end
		self._reactorPlays[reactor] = entry
		local live = state.place
		if state.place then
			entry.play:place()
		end
		local kickedBy = {}
		for _, record in ipairs(state.records) do
			if record.actsAs == "Impulse" then
				local struck, kicked = entry.play:strike(record)
				live = struck or live
				kickedBy[record] = kicked
			elseif not record.ended then
				live = entry.play:watch(record) or live
			end
		end
		if not live or not Entries.resume(self, entry) then
			Entries.discard(self, entry)
			return
		end
		-- The cut was made around the first of them; any other Impulse that came meanwhile
		-- cracks the ground again at its own place.
		if hit then
			Recrack.opened(entry, state.records, hit)
		end
		for _, record in ipairs(state.records) do
			Entries.crackAgain(self, entry, record, kickedBy[record])
			if entry.wounds then
				entry.wounds:strike(record)
			end
		end
	end)
	return state
end

-- The Reactor is being put back as built: nobody is owed an entry any more.
function Entries.forget(cutting)
	if cutting then
		table.clear(cutting.records)
		cutting.place = false
		cutting.emitCtx = nil
	end
end

function Entries.entryFor(self, reactor, emitCtx, record)
	local entry = self._reactorPlays[reactor]
	if entry then
		return entry
	end
	local cutting = self._reactorCutting[reactor]
	if cutting then
		return nil, cutting
	end
	local data = self:GetData(reactor)
	if not data then
		return nil
	end
	local sets = nil
	local hit = nil
	if cutByEngine(data) then
		local reach = nil
		if record and waitsForHit(data) then
			hit = record.field.origin.Position
			if data.ShardPattern == "Cracks" then
				reach = record.field.range
			end
		end
		local jobs
		sets, jobs = shardPlan(reactor, data, hit, reach, hasGrounds(data, emitCtx))
		if #jobs > 0 then
			return nil, startCutting(self, reactor, data, sets, jobs, hit)
		end
	end
	entry = newEntry(self, reactor, data, emitCtx, sets)
	self._reactorPlays[reactor] = entry
	-- The cut is around this Force's hit: it asks for no later crack at that place.
	if entry and hit then
		Recrack.opened(entry, { record }, hit)
	end
	return entry
end

-- Returns at once; the cut takes a few frames. Nothing to do for a Reactor that is out of
-- place, that the engine does not cut, or whose points gather around a hit that has not come.
function Entries.prepare(self, item)
	if self._reactorPlays[item] or self._reactorCutting[item] then
		return
	end
	local data = self:GetData(item)
	if not data or not cutByEngine(data) or waitsForHit(data) then
		return
	end
	local sets, jobs = shardPlan(item, data, nil, nil, false)
	if #jobs > 0 then
		startCutting(self, item, data, sets, jobs)
	end
end

return Entries

--[[
	Ground  -  one face of a block-shaped part as rectangles: what of it open cracks hold
	(Reactor/Wounds) and what is left intact. Numbers only, no instances.

	A place is (u, v) on the face, in studs from its middle. A rectangle is
	{ minU, minV, maxU, maxV }.

	Ground.new(halfU, halfV, snap) -> ground
	    snap: the least width of anything this makes. An edge nearer than that to an edge
	    already there is laid onto it, so no strip thinner than `snap` is ever left.
	ground:claim(owner, centreU, centreV, half) -> { rectangle }
	    The square of half-side `half` around the centre, cut to the face, less what is held
	    already. The rectangles returned are intact ground no longer: they are `owner`'s until
	    released. Empty when the square holds nothing intact.
	ground:release(owner)
	ground:held(owner) -> { rectangle }: what `owner` holds, or nil
	ground:touching(minU, minV, maxU, maxV) -> { owner }: whose rectangles overlap that area,
	    in the order they claimed
	ground:remainder(unshown) -> { rectangle }: the intact ground, as few large rectangles
	    unshown: nil, or a set of owners (owner -> true) whose rectangles still count as
	    intact: a crack that holds its ground while its pieces are being cut.
	ground:isWhole() -> boolean: nothing is held

	Every edge on an axis is `snap` or more from every other, the face's own two included:
	claim keeps that, and the grid of cells between the edges has no cell thinner than `snap`.
]]

local Ground = {}
Ground.__index = Ground

function Ground.new(halfU, halfV, snap)
	local self = setmetatable({}, Ground)
	self.halfU = halfU
	self.halfV = halfV
	self.snap = snap
	-- owner -> its rectangles, and the owners in the order they claimed.
	self.rectangles = {}
	self.owners = {}
	return self
end

-- Every edge on one axis: the face's two and those of every held rectangle.
local function edgesOf(self, minKey, maxKey, half)
	local edges = { -half, half }
	for _, owner in ipairs(self.owners) do
		for _, rectangle in ipairs(self.rectangles[owner]) do
			table.insert(edges, rectangle[minKey])
			table.insert(edges, rectangle[maxKey])
		end
	end
	return edges
end

-- `value`, laid onto the nearest of `edges` when one is nearer than `snap`.
local function snapped(value, edges, snap)
	local best = value
	local least = snap
	for _, edge in ipairs(edges) do
		local distance = math.abs(edge - value)
		if distance < least then
			least = distance
			best = edge
		end
	end
	return best
end

-- The distinct values of `edges` from `low` to `high`, both ends among them, in order, and the
-- place of each value in that list.
local function cuts(edges, low, high)
	local within = { low, high }
	for _, edge in ipairs(edges) do
		if edge > low and edge < high then
			table.insert(within, edge)
		end
	end
	table.sort(within)
	local distinct = {}
	local placeOf = {}
	for _, edge in ipairs(within) do
		if distinct[#distinct] ~= edge then
			table.insert(distinct, edge)
			placeOf[edge] = #distinct
		end
	end
	return distinct, placeOf
end

-- The part of an area that nobody holds, as rectangles. The held rectangles' edges make a grid
-- of cells over the area; the free cells are merged, row by row, into the largest rectangles
-- they give (greedy meshing). `unshown`: owners whose rectangles count as free.
local function freeIn(self, minU, minV, maxU, maxV, unshown)
	local us, columnOf = cuts(edgesOf(self, "minU", "maxU", self.halfU), minU, maxU)
	local vs, rowOf = cuts(edgesOf(self, "minV", "maxV", self.halfV), minV, maxV)
	local columns = #us - 1
	local rows = #vs - 1

	local taken = {}
	for _, owner in ipairs(self.owners) do
		local counted = self.rectangles[owner]
		if unshown and unshown[owner] then
			counted = {}
		end
		for _, rectangle in ipairs(counted) do
			local overlaps = rectangle.minU < maxU and rectangle.maxU > minU and rectangle.minV < maxV and rectangle.maxV > minV
			if overlaps then
				local firstColumn = columnOf[math.max(rectangle.minU, minU)]
				local lastColumn = columnOf[math.min(rectangle.maxU, maxU)] - 1
				local firstRow = rowOf[math.max(rectangle.minV, minV)]
				local lastRow = rowOf[math.min(rectangle.maxV, maxV)] - 1
				for row = firstRow, lastRow do
					for column = firstColumn, lastColumn do
						taken[(row - 1) * columns + column] = true
					end
				end
			end
		end
	end

	local rectangles = {}
	for row = 1, rows do
		for column = 1, columns do
			if not taken[(row - 1) * columns + column] then
				local lastColumn = column
				while lastColumn < columns and not taken[(row - 1) * columns + lastColumn + 1] do
					lastColumn += 1
				end
				local lastRow = row
				local grows = true
				while grows and lastRow < rows do
					for across = column, lastColumn do
						if taken[lastRow * columns + across] then
							grows = false
							break
						end
					end
					if grows then
						lastRow += 1
					end
				end
				for filled = row, lastRow do
					for across = column, lastColumn do
						taken[(filled - 1) * columns + across] = true
					end
				end
				table.insert(rectangles, { minU = us[column], minV = vs[row], maxU = us[lastColumn + 1], maxV = vs[lastRow + 1] })
			end
		end
	end
	return rectangles
end

function Ground:claim(owner, centreU, centreV, half)
	local snap = self.snap
	local uEdges = edgesOf(self, "minU", "maxU", self.halfU)
	local vEdges = edgesOf(self, "minV", "maxV", self.halfV)
	local minU = snapped(math.max(centreU - half, -self.halfU), uEdges, snap)
	local maxU = snapped(math.min(centreU + half, self.halfU), uEdges, snap)
	local minV = snapped(math.max(centreV - half, -self.halfV), vEdges, snap)
	local maxV = snapped(math.min(centreV + half, self.halfV), vEdges, snap)
	if maxU - minU < snap or maxV - minV < snap then
		return {}
	end
	local rectangles = freeIn(self, minU, minV, maxU, maxV)
	if #rectangles == 0 then
		return rectangles
	end
	local own = self.rectangles[owner]
	if not own then
		self.rectangles[owner] = rectangles
		table.insert(self.owners, owner)
		return rectangles
	end
	for _, rectangle in ipairs(rectangles) do
		table.insert(own, rectangle)
	end
	return rectangles
end

function Ground:release(owner)
	if not self.rectangles[owner] then
		return
	end
	self.rectangles[owner] = nil
	table.remove(self.owners, table.find(self.owners, owner))
end

function Ground:held(owner)
	return self.rectangles[owner]
end

function Ground:touching(minU, minV, maxU, maxV)
	local found = {}
	for _, owner in ipairs(self.owners) do
		for _, rectangle in ipairs(self.rectangles[owner]) do
			if rectangle.minU < maxU and rectangle.maxU > minU and rectangle.minV < maxV and rectangle.maxV > minV then
				table.insert(found, owner)
				break
			end
		end
	end
	return found
end

function Ground:remainder(unshown)
	return freeIn(self, -self.halfU, -self.halfV, self.halfU, self.halfV, unshown)
end

function Ground:isWhole()
	return #self.owners == 0
end

return Ground

--[[
	GroundDisplay  -  what is left intact of a ground that has open cracks (Reactor/Wounds):
	plain boxes around the wounds, in the ground's look, while the ground itself is hidden.

	The ground is LIVE user content. It is written in one way only, Reactor/Display's hide and
	show, once per ground however many wounds are open, and it stays solid: what is thrown out
	of a wound lands on it, and nobody falls through a crater. The boxes are copies that are
	not saved (Archivable off, under the runtime's folder, marked _PartIcleEmit) and that
	nothing collides with.

	A tiling Texture on the struck face is carried onto the boxes, its offset moved so the
	pattern runs on across them. Measured in Studio for the top face only: a Texture is laid
	from the face's +X and +Z edges. On another face the boxes carry no Texture. A Decal is
	stretched over its whole face and cannot be carried at all.

	GroundDisplay.new(folder, onServer) -> display
	display.draw(ground, rectangles, face)
	    ground: { part, frame, size } (Reactor/Wounds). rectangles: the intact rest of its
	    face `face` ({ axis, side }), each { minU, minV, maxU, maxV } (Reactor/Ground); the
	    boxes are those rectangles through the ground. nil: the ground is whole again, its
	    boxes go and it is shown.
	display.clear()   every ground whole again
]]

local EngineAttr = require(script.Parent.Parent.EngineAttr)
local Display = require(script.Parent.Display)
local Index = require(script.Parent.Index)
local Sites = require(script.Parent.Sites)

local GroundDisplay = {}

-- A bare copy of the ground, to be sized as one box of it.
local function makeBox(part, folder, shown)
	local box = Instance.fromExisting(part)
	box.Name = "GroundBox"
	box.Archivable = false
	box.Anchored = true
	box.CanCollide = false
	box.CanQuery = false
	box.CanTouch = false
	box.Locked = true
	-- On a server the ground is hidden through its own Transparency, which the copy took.
	if shown then
		box.Transparency = shown.Transparency
	end
	Index.unmark(box)
	box:SetAttribute("_PartIcleEmit", true)
	box.Parent = folder
	return box
end

-- The ground's Textures that tile its struck face, when that face is one they can be carried on.
local function carried(part, face)
	local textures = {}
	if face.axis ~= "Y" or face.side ~= 1 then
		return textures
	end
	for _, child in ipairs(part:GetChildren()) do
		if child:IsA("Texture") and child.Face == Enum.NormalId.Top then
			table.insert(textures, child)
		end
	end
	return textures
end

function GroundDisplay.new(folder, onServer)
	-- part -> { boxes, kept (what Display.show puts back), textures }
	local drawn = {}
	local display = {}

	local function whole(part)
		local state = drawn[part]
		if not state then
			return
		end
		drawn[part] = nil
		for _, box in ipairs(state.boxes) do
			box:Destroy()
		end
		Display.show(part, onServer, state.kept)
	end

	function display.draw(ground, rectangles, face)
		local part = ground.part
		if not rectangles then
			whole(part)
			return
		end
		local state = drawn[part]
		if not state then
			-- The Textures are read before the ground is hidden: hiding writes them too.
			state = { boxes = {}, textures = carried(part, face) }
			drawn[part] = state
		end
		local boxes = state.boxes
		for position = #boxes, #rectangles + 1, -1 do
			boxes[position]:Destroy()
			boxes[position] = nil
		end
		local thickness = ground.size[face.axis]
		for position, rectangle in ipairs(rectangles) do
			local box = boxes[position]
			if not box then
				box = makeBox(part, folder, onServer and state.kept or nil)
				for _, texture in ipairs(state.textures) do
					local copy = texture:Clone()
					-- The ground's own Texture is hidden with it: the copy is not.
					EngineAttr.writeProp(copy, "LocalTransparencyModifier", 0)
					copy.Parent = box
				end
				boxes[position] = box
			end
			local centre = Sites.alongFace(face.axis, (rectangle.minU + rectangle.maxU) / 2, (rectangle.minV + rectangle.maxV) / 2, 0)
			box.Size = Sites.alongFace(face.axis, rectangle.maxU - rectangle.minU, rectangle.maxV - rectangle.minV, thickness)
			box.CFrame = ground.frame * CFrame.new(centre.X, centre.Y, centre.Z)
			if #state.textures > 0 then
				local copies = {}
				for _, child in ipairs(box:GetChildren()) do
					if child:IsA("Texture") then
						table.insert(copies, child)
					end
				end
				for place, texture in ipairs(state.textures) do
					copies[place].OffsetStudsU = texture.OffsetStudsU + ground.size.X / 2 - rectangle.maxU
					copies[place].OffsetStudsV = texture.OffsetStudsV + ground.size.Z / 2 - rectangle.maxV
				end
			end
		end
		-- Hidden last, so the boxes are there in the frame the ground goes.
		if not state.kept then
			state.kept = Display.hide(part, onServer, true)
		end
	end

	function display.clear()
		for part in pairs(table.clone(drawn)) do
			whole(part)
		end
	end

	return display
end

return GroundDisplay

--[[
	Index  -  which Reactors a Force could reach. A Reactor is found by its tag (set by
	TransformReactor), so nothing is scanned: a place with no Reactors costs one empty list.
	Index.reaches is a first, generous test (a ball around the Reactor against a ball around
	the Force's shape); Reactor/Play decides piece by piece.
	Index.unmark makes a copy of a Reactor an ordinary instance again (Reactor/Display's
	stand-ins, the plugin's Modules/Scatter).
]]

local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService")

local Index = {}

Index.TAG = "PartIcleReactor"
-- The item attributes TransformReactor (Reactor/init.luau) stamps; one added there is added here.
Index.MARKS = { "Transformed", "Qwinkle", "IsReactor", "IsEmitter", "EmitCount", "EmitDuration", "EmitDelay", "EmissionMode", "AnimateLoop" }

-- Every tagged Reactor that is in the world right now.
function Index.reactors()
	local found = {}
	for _, reactor in ipairs(CollectionService:GetTagged(Index.TAG)) do
		if reactor:IsDescendantOf(workspace) and not reactor:GetAttribute("_PartIcleEmit") then
			table.insert(found, reactor)
		end
	end
	return found
end

-- The farthest any point of a field's shape is from its origin.
function Index.reachOf(field)
	if field.shape == "Linear" then
		return math.sqrt(field.range * field.range + field.halfWidth * field.halfWidth + field.halfHeight * field.halfHeight)
	elseif field.shape == "Vortex" then
		return math.sqrt(field.range * field.range + field.height * field.height)
	end
	return field.range
end

function Index.reaches(field, centre, radius)
	return (centre - field.origin.Position).Magnitude <= radius + Index.reachOf(field)
end

-- Takes a Reactor's attributes and tag off a COPY of one. Never called on the Reactor itself.
function Index.unmark(copy)
	for _, mark in ipairs(Index.MARKS) do
		copy:SetAttribute(mark, nil)
	end
	copy:RemoveTag(Index.TAG)
end

-- A Force's Group reaches a Reactor when it is empty or the same.
function Index.groupMatches(forceGroup, reactorGroup)
	return forceGroup == "" or forceGroup == reactorGroup
end

return Index

--[[
	Patches  -  the engine's cut of the patches of a ground (Reactor/Wounds). A patch is not a
	part of the place: it is a rectangle of a ground's face, through the ground. So each is cut
	from a template, a plain block of the patch's size that is never put into the world, by the
	cut cracked ground always gets (Reactor/Shards: the crust off its base, the crust in rings
	around the hit).

	A shard's box is its place in the template's own space, so it does not matter where the
	template stands: Reactor/Wounds stands the pieces where the patch is.

	A whole square (job.whole) is the same cut every time for one size, Range and variant, so
	its shards are kept and the next such crack is answered at once, in the frame of its
	Force. Kept shards are templates only: every wound copies its own stand-ins from them
	(Reactor/Display), so any number of open wounds share one kept cut. The least recently
	used go when more than KEPT are held; a wound that still uses them holds on to them.

	Patches.cut(jobs, done)
	    jobs: { { size, hit, reach, count, seed, face, whole, variant }, ... } (Reactor/Wounds:
	    hit in the template's space, face = { axis, side }). done(sets) is called when every
	    job is answered, sets[position] the shards of that job (Reactor/Shards) or false when
	    it asks for fewer than two pieces or the engine gave none. With every job kept, done is
	    called before cut returns; otherwise a few frames later.
	Patches.kept() -> how many cuts are held
	Patches.forget()  drops them all
]]

local Shards = require(script.Parent.Shards)

-- The kept cuts held at most.
local KEPT = 12

local Patches = {}

-- key -> { shards, used }: the cuts of whole squares, and when each was last asked for.
local kept = {}
local held = 0
local uses = 0

local function keyOf(job)
	local size = job.size
	return string.format("%.2f,%.2f,%.2f|%d|%.2f|%s%d|%d", size.X, size.Y, size.Z, job.count, job.reach, job.face.axis, job.face.side, job.variant)
end

local function remember(key, shards)
	uses += 1
	if not kept[key] then
		held += 1
	end
	kept[key] = { shards = shards, used = uses }
	while held > KEPT do
		local oldest, least = nil, math.huge
		for name, entry in pairs(kept) do
			if entry.used < least then
				oldest, least = name, entry.used
			end
		end
		kept[oldest] = nil
		held -= 1
	end
end

function Patches.cut(jobs, done)
	local sets = table.create(#jobs, false)
	local cuts = {}
	for position, job in ipairs(jobs) do
		local key = nil
		if job.whole then
			key = keyOf(job)
		end
		local known = key and kept[key]
		if known then
			uses += 1
			known.used = uses
			sets[position] = known.shards
		elseif job.count >= 2 then
			local template = Instance.new("Part")
			template.Anchored = true
			template.Size = job.size
			-- A kept cut is drawn from its variant alone, so every Force of that size gets it.
			local seed = job.seed
			if key then
				seed = (job.variant + 1) * 104729
			end
			table.insert(cuts, {
				part = template,
				key = Shards.key(template, job.count, seed, job.hit, job.reach, false),
				count = job.count,
				seed = seed,
				hit = job.hit,
				reach = job.reach,
				face = job.face,
				loose = true,
				position = position,
				keep = key,
			})
		end
	end
	Shards.prepare(cuts, function()
		for _, cut in ipairs(cuts) do
			local shards = Shards.get(cut.part, cut.key) or false
			sets[cut.position] = shards
			if cut.keep and shards then
				remember(cut.keep, shards)
			end
			cut.part:Destroy()
		end
		done(sets)
	end)
end

function Patches.kept()
	return held
end

function Patches.forget()
	kept = {}
	held = 0
end

return Patches

--[[
	Pieces  -  the parts of a Reactor that can be pushed, as records for Reactor/Play:
	{ part, rest (its CFrame now), halfExt, size, reach }.
	A Model has every BasePart under it; a Reactor that is one part has itself and every
	BasePart under it (Modules/Scatter places copies there). A transformed item inside (an
	emitter with its own RenderTemplate) keeps to itself and is skipped with everything under
	it. Read each time a play starts, so hand edits are picked up.

	With Break = "Blocks" a part is cut into about `pieceCount` blocks (fewer for a very small
	part: Reactor/Sites.count). A plain block-shaped Part is cut here, by arithmetic
	(Reactor/Dice.cut): one record per block, with the same part, blockSize (the block's own
	size), and siblings, one list shared by all the blocks of that part, holding their places in
	the returned array. Any other part is cut by the engine around an even grid of points, and
	its blocks come as shards do (below); one the caller has no shards for stays one piece.
	The cut is the same every time for the same Reactor: each part draws from its own seed.

	With Break = "Shards" a part gives one record per shard the caller has for it:
	shardsOf(part) -> { { template, box, size, standOffset, fixed }, ... } (Reactor/Shards) or
	nil for a part that moves whole. A record's rest is the shard's own box, in the world; it
	carries shard (the template its stand-in is copied from), standOffset and siblings as a
	block does, box (the shard's box in the part's space) and siteIndex and sites (the point it
	was cut around, as its place among the points of the cut; Reactor/Recut finds by them the
	piece a point falls in). Of a part cut as cracked ground (the set has a strike), a base
	shard's record is fixed, and every other record carries strike = { origin, normal, reach,
	crust } in the world, one table for the whole part (Reactor/Crack reads it).

	Pieces.parts(reactor) -> the parts collect reads, in its order: the Reactor itself when it
	is a part, then every BasePart under it outside transformed items.
	Pieces.isPlainBlock(part) -> true for a Part whose Shape is Block and that carries no mesh:
	the one kind Break = "Blocks" cuts without the engine.

	Pieces.ofShard(part, rest, shard) -> the record of one shard standing at `rest`, without the
	marks of its set (siblings, strike, sites): Reactor/Recut makes the pieces of a later cut by it.
	Pieces.ofSet(pieces, part, frame, shards, siblings, cut) -> siblings
	    Adds one record per shard of a set to `pieces`, standing where the space the set was cut
	    in stands (`frame`). siblings: the list the records join, when the set shows together
	    with others; made when nil. cut = { size, face = { axis, side } } when that space is not
	    the part itself but a patch of it (Reactor/Wounds): every record carries it, and one
	    whose box meets a side of the patch is marked atEdge (Reactor/Crack leaves it at rest
	    beyond the rim, so the patch's outline never shows against the ground around it).
	Pieces.touchesSide(box, halfExt, cut) -> whether a box of the patch's space meets its side
	Pieces.ofBlock(part, rest, size) -> the record of one uncut block of a part

	Pieces.carry(pieces, own, origin, fullPose) moves the records of a Reactor that is emitted
	somewhere else (EmitAt, an event) to that place: the parts themselves stay where they are.
]]

local Dice = require(script.Parent.Dice)
local Sites = require(script.Parent.Sites)

local Pieces = {}

-- size: the edge of a cube of the volume, what a Force's Size Response goes by.
-- reach: the longest edge.
local function record(part, rest, size)
	return {
		part = part,
		rest = rest,
		halfExt = size / 2,
		size = (size.X * size.Y * size.Z) ^ (1 / 3),
		reach = math.max(size.X, size.Y, size.Z),
	}
end

-- A plain box: a Part whose Shape is Block and that carries no mesh of its own.
function Pieces.isPlainBlock(part)
	if part.ClassName ~= "Part" or part.Shape ~= Enum.PartType.Block then
		return false
	end
	for _, child in ipairs(part:GetChildren()) do
		if child:IsA("DataModelMesh") then
			return false
		end
	end
	return true
end

-- One whole block of a part, standing at `rest`: what Reactor/Display draws as a box of that
-- size in the part's look.
function Pieces.ofBlock(part, rest, size)
	local piece = record(part, rest, size)
	piece.blockSize = size
	return piece
end

function Pieces.ofShard(part, rest, shard)
	local piece = record(part, rest, shard.size)
	piece.shard = shard.template
	piece.standOffset = shard.standOffset
	piece.box = shard.box
	piece.siteIndex = shard.siteIndex
	return piece
end

-- A box this near a side of its patch meets it.
local EDGE_SLACK = 0.05

function Pieces.touchesSide(box, halfExt, cut)
	local alongX = box:VectorToWorldSpace(Vector3.new(halfExt.X, 0, 0))
	local alongY = box:VectorToWorldSpace(Vector3.new(0, halfExt.Y, 0))
	local alongZ = box:VectorToWorldSpace(Vector3.new(0, 0, halfExt.Z))
	local uAxis, vAxis = Sites.faceAxes(cut.face.axis)
	for _, axis in ipairs({ uAxis, vAxis }) do
		local reach = math.abs(alongX[axis]) + math.abs(alongY[axis]) + math.abs(alongZ[axis])
		if math.abs(box.Position[axis]) + reach > cut.size[axis] / 2 - EDGE_SLACK then
			return true
		end
	end
	return false
end

function Pieces.ofSet(pieces, part, frame, shards, siblings, cut)
	local strike = nil
	if shards.strike then
		strike = {
			origin = frame:PointToWorldSpace(shards.strike.origin),
			normal = frame:VectorToWorldSpace(shards.strike.normal),
			reach = shards.strike.reach,
			crust = shards.strike.crust,
		}
	end
	siblings = siblings or table.create(#shards)
	for _, shard in ipairs(shards) do
		local piece = Pieces.ofShard(part, frame * shard.box, shard)
		piece.siblings = siblings
		piece.cut = cut
		if shard.fixed then
			piece.fixed = true
		else
			piece.strike = strike
			piece.sites = shards.sites
			if cut and Pieces.touchesSide(shard.box, piece.halfExt, cut) then
				piece.atEdge = true
			end
		end
		table.insert(pieces, piece)
		table.insert(siblings, #pieces)
	end
	return siblings
end

-- One record per shard of a part, or false when the caller has none for it.
local function addShards(pieces, part, shardsOf)
	local shards = shardsOf and shardsOf(part) or nil
	if not shards or #shards < 2 then
		return false
	end
	Pieces.ofSet(pieces, part, part.CFrame, shards)
	return true
end

local function add(pieces, part, breakMode, pieceCount, shardsOf)
	local plainBlock = breakMode == "Blocks" and Pieces.isPlainBlock(part)
	-- Shards, and the blocks of a part that is not a plain box, are the engine's fragments.
	local fromEngine = breakMode == "Shards" or (breakMode == "Blocks" and not plainBlock)
	if fromEngine and addShards(pieces, part, shardsOf) then
		return
	end
	if not plainBlock then
		table.insert(pieces, record(part, part.CFrame, part.Size))
		return
	end
	local blocks = Dice.cut(part.Size, Sites.count(part.Size, pieceCount), Sites.sequence(#pieces * 7919 + 13))
	if #blocks == 1 then
		table.insert(pieces, record(part, part.CFrame, part.Size))
		return
	end
	local siblings = table.create(#blocks)
	for _, block in ipairs(blocks) do
		local piece = record(part, part.CFrame * CFrame.new(block.offset.X, block.offset.Y, block.offset.Z), block.size)
		piece.blockSize = block.size
		piece.siblings = siblings
		table.insert(pieces, piece)
		table.insert(siblings, #pieces)
	end
end

local function visit(parent, parts)
	for _, child in ipairs(parent:GetChildren()) do
		if not child:GetAttribute("Transformed") then
			if child:IsA("BasePart") and not child:IsA("Terrain") then
				table.insert(parts, child)
			end
			visit(child, parts)
		end
	end
end

function Pieces.parts(reactor)
	local parts = {}
	if reactor:IsA("BasePart") then
		table.insert(parts, reactor)
	end
	visit(reactor, parts)
	return parts
end

-- Rewrites every rest pose for a Reactor whose frame is `own` and that is emitted at `origin`.
-- A full pose brings the layout into the origin's frame; otherwise it is only moved there and
-- every piece keeps its rotation.
function Pieces.carry(pieces, own, origin, fullPose)
	-- A strike is shared by the pieces of its crack: it is moved once.
	local strikes = {}
	for _, piece in ipairs(pieces) do
		if piece.strike then
			strikes[piece.strike] = true
		end
	end
	if fullPose then
		for _, piece in ipairs(pieces) do
			piece.rest = origin * own:ToObjectSpace(piece.rest)
		end
		for strike in pairs(strikes) do
			strike.origin = origin:PointToWorldSpace(own:PointToObjectSpace(strike.origin))
			strike.normal = origin:VectorToWorldSpace(own:VectorToObjectSpace(strike.normal))
		end
		return
	end
	local shift = origin.Position - own.Position
	for _, piece in ipairs(pieces) do
		piece.rest = piece.rest + shift
	end
	for strike in pairs(strikes) do
		strike.origin = strike.origin + shift
	end
end

-- leftOut(part) -> true for a part that gives no records: a ground, whose cracks are
-- wounds of their own (Reactor/Wounds).
function Pieces.collect(reactor, breakMode, pieceCount, shardsOf, leftOut)
	local pieces = {}
	for _, part in ipairs(Pieces.parts(reactor)) do
		if not (leftOut and leftOut(part)) then
			add(pieces, part, breakMode, pieceCount or 50, shardsOf)
		end
	end
	return pieces
end

return Pieces

--[[
	Play  -  one disturbed Reactor: which pieces are out of place, on what paths, and what happens
	once they have all come to rest (the Fade and the Return are Reactor/After). Logic only: instances are reached through `display`
