	(Reactor/Display in the runtime, a recorder in the tests) and the world through `castRay`, so
	all of it runs under the luau CLI.

	A piece is { rest = CFrame, halfExt = Vector3, size = number, reach = number }.
	States: RESTING (never pushed: the original stands, the play shows nothing for it), FLYING
	(on a path), LANDED (its path ended; it lies where it fell), GONE (sunk away or lost), DRIVEN
	(carried by a Continuous Force: Reactor/Driven steps it live until no Force holds it).

	A pushed piece flies a path from Rocks/Trajectory: a plain arc at once, replaced by the whole
	built path (bounces, roll-out, rest pose) within the per-frame build budget. A push on a piece
	already out of place rebuilds its path from where it is and how fast it goes.

	A Force's strength is a distance: how far, in studs, it throws a piece (Fields.throwSpeed
	turns it into a speed under the piece's own gravity). Hold is a distance too: a throw no
	longer than Hold leaves the piece standing.

	With settings.Collapse, a piece left standing with no chain of standing neighbours to
	something that carries it (Reactor/Support) is let go and falls. The graph is built the first
	time a piece of the play wakes.

	Cracked ground (Reactor/Crack): a piece that is fixed (the base under the crust) is never
	pushed, by a Force or by a collapse. A crust piece (it carries a strike) that an Impulse
	reaches and does not throw is stood a little out of place instead: sunk and tipped in the
	crater, heaved on the rim, moved by a hair beyond; outside the crater no Force throws it.
	Such a piece stays RESTING. A Continuous Force cracks nothing. A later Impulse elsewhere on
	the same ground cracks it again (Reactor/Recut): pieces are added to the play while it runs,
	and a piece that was cut again is retired (piece.retired, GONE for good).

	settings: Hold, HoldSpread, Collapse, isAnchored(index) (asked once per piece when Collapse
	is on), After ("Stay" | "Fade" | "Return"), AfterDelay, AfterTime, closes (a wound of a
	ground: a Fade ends with the ground grown back and the play done, Reactor/After.close),
	MaxPieces, MaxAirTime (seconds a piece may fly: its path looks for ground that long, and
	one still in the air after it is taken away; never less than a second),
	wakeBudget (stand-ins made per frame), buildBudget (paths built per frame), and
	the functions rollGravity(),
	rollBounciness(), rollFriction(), rollTumble() (radians per second) and random() (0 to 1).
	display: wake(index) shows a stand-in for a piece, hides the original and returns how many
	stand-ins it made (a block brings its siblings); move(indices, frames, count) places stand-ins; drop(index) removes one for good; restore(index) removes it
	and shows the original again.

	A play can be placed (Play:place): every piece is given its stand-in at once and stands at
	rest, for a Reactor emitted somewhere other than where its parts are. Nothing moves until a
	Force pushes; a pushed piece then goes at once, its stand-in being there already, and a
	Return ends with the Reactor standing at that place again.

	step(dt) returns "active" while anything moves or is still to come, "dormant" when the pieces
	lie where they fell and nothing more happens without a new Force, and "done" when every piece
	is back at rest and the play can be thrown away.
]]

local Trajectory = require(script.Parent.Parent.Rocks.Trajectory)
local Fields = require(script.Parent.Parent.Force.Fields)
local Driven = require(script.Parent.Driven)
local Support = require(script.Parent.Support)
local After = require(script.Parent.After)
local Crack = require(script.Parent.Crack)

local RESTING = 0
local FLYING = 1
local LANDED = 2
local GONE = 3
local DRIVEN = Driven.STATE

local ZERO = Vector3.new(0, 0, 0)
local UP = Vector3.new(0, 1, 0)
local TINY = 1e-4
-- The least a play's Max Air Time counts as.
local LEAST_AIR_TIME = 1
-- How far above a surface a piece buried past its middle starts its flight.
local SURFACE_MARGIN = 0.02

local Play = {}
Play.__index = Play

function Play.new(pieces, settings, display, castRay)
	local self = setmetatable({}, Play)
	self.pieces = pieces
	self.settings = settings
	self.display = display
	self.castRay = castRay
	-- A piece whose built path meets no ground within this many seconds is taken away then.
	self.airTime = math.max(settings.MaxAirTime, LEAST_AIR_TIME)
	-- Rocks/Trajectory.build's rules for a piece: it leaves walls, it starts where it stood, on
	-- the ground or sunk into it, which a Rocks chunk does not, and ground is looked for all
	-- through its air time.
	self.pathRules = { offWalls = true, fromRest = true, airTime = self.airTime }
	self.clock = 0
	self.state = table.create(#pieces, RESTING)
	-- Per piece, set at its first launch.
	self.path = {}
	self.pathStart = {}
	self.pathBuilt = {}
	self.gravity = {}
	self.bounciness = {}
	self.friction = {}
	self.lastFrame = {}
	self.landedAfter = {}
	self.holdOf = {}
	-- Reactor/Support's graph, and whether pieces have left since it was last walked.
	self.support = nil
	self.supportStale = false
	-- record -> the pieces it has already reached.
	self.kicks = {}
	self.flying = {}
	-- The pieces a Continuous Force carries, and their live state (Reactor/Driven).
	self.driven = {}
	-- index -> the way a Continuous Force carried the piece (Reactor/Driven).
	self.track = {}
	self.drivePosition = {}
	self.driveRotation = {}
	self.driveVelocity = {}
	self.driveSpin = {}
	self.pendingWake = {}
	self.pendingPush = {}
	-- Cracked ground (Reactor/Crack): the pieces queued or stood out of place, and their poses.
	self.cracked = {}
	self.crackFrame = {}
	self.pendingCrack = {}
	-- record -> true while a later crack of its own is being cut (Reactor/Recrack): until it
	-- is in, that Force leaves the standing crust alone, and then kicks it late (kickAgain).
	self.recracking = {}
	self.buildQueue = {}
	self.moveIndices = {}
	self.moveFrames = {}
	self.moveCount = 0
	-- Pieces with a stand-in, and pieces whose original is hidden (a faded piece is still hidden).
	self.awake = 0
	self.hidden = 0
	-- True once Play:place has stood every piece up as a stand-in.
	self.placed = false
	self.phase = "live"
	self.phaseTime = 0
	self.idleFor = 0
	-- The time sources of the Forces that have moved a piece of this play (Force/Registry:
	-- record.time, a Container's, and record.ownTime, the Force's own Timescale). Reactor/init
	-- steps the play by the slowest of them.
	self.times = {}
	return self
end

-- Starts following a Force. False while the play is fading or returning: those finish first.
function Play:watch(record)
	if self.phase ~= "live" then
		return false
	end
	if not self.kicks[record] then
		self.kicks[record] = {}
	end
	self.idleFor = 0
	return true
end

-- The kick of an Impulse that arrived before this play existed, given NOW: a Reactor whose
-- shards were still being cut (Reactor/init) answers late. An Impulse lasts a frame or two, so
-- one that is merely followed can be over before this play's first step and its kick lost.
-- One still alive is followed as well, and remembers the pieces it has kicked here.
-- Returns true and the list of the pieces it kicked, which a later crack asks for (kickAgain).
function Play:strike(record)
	if self.phase ~= "live" then
		return false
	end
	local kicked = {}
	if not record.ended and self:watch(record) then
		kicked = self.kicks[record]
	end
	self:_applyImpulse(record, kicked)
	self.idleFor = 0
	return true, kicked
end

-- The kick of an Impulse, given to pieces it has passed by: a later crack (Reactor/Recut) made
-- them or took them over after the Impulse arrived. `kicked` is that Impulse's own list of the
-- pieces it has kicked here, kept by whoever asked for the crack; no other piece is kicked twice.
function Play:kickAgain(record, kicked, indices)
	if self.phase ~= "live" then
		return
	end
	for _, index in ipairs(indices) do
		kicked[index] = nil
	end
	self:_applyImpulse(record, kicked)
	self.idleFor = 0
end

-- A Force that moves a piece of this play lends the play its time. Following one is not
-- enough: a play out of place follows every Force of its Group, however far away.
function Play:_takeTime(record)
	local times = self.times
	local carried = record.time
	if carried and not table.find(times, carried) then
		table.insert(times, carried)
	end
	local own = record.ownTime
	if own and not table.find(times, own) then
		table.insert(times, own)
	end
end

function Play:_position(index)
	if self.state[index] == RESTING then
		return self.pieces[index].rest.Position
	end
	return self.lastFrame[index].Position
end

local function randomAxis(random)
	local axis = Vector3.new(random() * 2 - 1, random() * 2 - 1, random() * 2 - 1)
	if axis.Magnitude < TINY then
		return UP
	end
	return axis.Unit
end

-- A piece's own Hold: the Reactor's, spread by HoldSpread, rolled the first time it is asked for.
function Play:_holdOf(index)
	local hold = self.holdOf[index]
	if hold == nil then
		local settings = self.settings
		hold = settings.Hold * (1 + settings.HoldSpread * (settings.random() * 2 - 1))
		self.holdOf[index] = hold
	end
	return hold
end

-- A piece's own gravity, bounciness and friction, rolled the first time they are asked for.
function Play:_rolled(index)
	local settings = self.settings
	if self.gravity[index] == nil then
		self.gravity[index] = settings.rollGravity()
		self.bounciness[index] = settings.rollBounciness()
		self.friction[index] = settings.rollFriction()
	end
	return self.gravity[index]
end

-- Puts a piece on a plain arc from `frame` and queues the whole path for building.
function Play:_launch(index, frame, velocity, spin)
	local settings = self.settings
	-- Only a flight that starts where a Force let the piece go has that Force's way before it.
	local track = self.track[index]
	if track and not track.kept then
		self.track[index] = nil
	elseif track then
		track.kept = nil
	end
	self:_rolled(index)
	if spin.Magnitude < TINY then
		spin = randomAxis(settings.random) * settings.rollTumble()
	end
	self.path[index] = Trajectory.ballistic(frame.Position, velocity, frame.Rotation, spin)
	self.pathStart[index] = self.clock
	self.pathBuilt[index] = false
	self.lastFrame[index] = frame
	table.insert(self.buildQueue, index)
	if self.state[index] ~= FLYING then
		self.state[index] = FLYING
		table.insert(self.flying, index)
	end
end

-- Where a resting piece starts its flight. One buried past its middle starts just above the
-- surface it lies in: a ray cast from inside the ground does not find it.
function Play:_surfaced(index)
	local piece = self.pieces[index]
	local rest = piece.rest
	local reach = Support.worldHalf(piece).Y + SURFACE_MARGIN
	local over = self.castRay(rest.Position + UP * reach, UP * -reach)
	if not over then
		return rest
	end
	return rest + UP * (over.Position.Y - rest.Position.Y + SURFACE_MARGIN)
end

-- A push on one piece. A resting piece waits for its stand-in; a moving one is re-launched now.
function Play:_push(index, push)
	local state = self.state[index]
	if state == GONE or self.pieces[index].fixed then
		return
	end
	if state == RESTING then
		if self.placed then
			-- Its stand-in stands there already: it goes now, and counts against no cap.
			self:_launch(index, self:_surfaced(index), push, ZERO)
			self.supportStale = true
			return
		end
		if self.pendingPush[index] then
			self.pendingPush[index] += push
			return
		end
		if self.awake + #self.pendingWake >= self.settings.MaxPieces then
			return
		end
		self.pendingPush[index] = push
		table.insert(self.pendingWake, index)
		return
	end
	if state == DRIVEN then
		self.driveVelocity[index] += push
		return
	end
	local elapsed = self.clock - self.pathStart[index]
	local gravity = self.gravity[index]
	local frame = Trajectory.evaluate(self.path[index], elapsed, gravity)
	local velocity, spin = Trajectory.velocity(self.path[index], elapsed, gravity)
	self:_launch(index, frame, velocity + push, spin)
end

-- One kick for every piece the front of an Impulse has reached since the last frame.
function Play:_applyImpulse(record, kicked)
	local settings = self.settings
	local field = record.field
	local front = record.front
	local strength = record.strength
	local pulls = strength < 0
	local waits = self.recracking[record]
	for index, piece in ipairs(self.pieces) do
		local standsBy = waits and piece.strike ~= nil and self.state[index] == RESTING
		if not kicked[index] and self.state[index] ~= GONE and not piece.fixed and not standsBy then
			local direction, distance, distance01 = Fields.sample(field, self:_position(index), pulls)
			if direction and distance <= front then
				kicked[index] = true
				local share = Fields.sizeShare(piece.size, record.sizeResponse)
				local spread = 1 + record.variation * (settings.random() * 2 - 1)
				local throw = strength * Fields.kept(record.falloff, distance01) * share * spread
				if math.abs(throw) > self:_holdOf(index) and not Crack.holds(piece) then
					self:_push(index, direction * Fields.throwSpeed(throw, self:_rolled(index)))
					self:_takeTime(record)
				elseif piece.strike then
					Crack.strike(self, index)
				end
			end
		end
	end
end

function Play:_followForces()
	for record, kicked in pairs(self.kicks) do
		if record.ended then
			self.kicks[record] = nil
		elseif record.actsAs == "Impulse" then
			self:_applyImpulse(record, kicked)
		else
			Driven.capture(self, record)
		end
	end
end

-- Stand-ins for the pieces waiting to move, until the frame's budget of new stand-ins is spent.
function Play:_wakePending()
	local pending = self.pendingWake
	local budget = self.settings.wakeBudget
	local taken = 0
	local made = 0
	while taken < #pending and made < budget do
		taken += 1
		local index = pending[taken]
		local push = self.pendingPush[index]
		self.pendingPush[index] = nil
		made += self.display.wake(index) or 1
		self.awake += 1
		self.hidden += 1
		-- A cracked piece flies from where it was stood.
		self:_launch(index, self.crackFrame[index] or self:_surfaced(index), push, ZERO)
	end
	if taken == 0 then
		return
	end
	self.supportStale = true
	local remaining = {}
	for position = taken + 1, #pending do
		table.insert(remaining, pending[position])
	end
	self.pendingWake = remaining
end

-- Lets go of every standing piece that has lost its last chain to something that carries it.
-- Those wake over the next frames like any other, and may bring more down in their turn.
function Play:_collapse()
	self.supportStale = false
	local settings = self.settings
	if not settings.Collapse then
		return
	end
	if not self.support then
		self.support = Support.build(self.pieces, settings.isAnchored)
	end
	local fallen = Support.unsupported(self.support, function(index)
		return self.state[index] == RESTING and self.pendingPush[index] == nil
	end)
	for _, index in ipairs(fallen) do
		self:_push(index, ZERO)
	end
end

-- Whole paths in place of plain arcs, as many as the frame's budget allows.
function Play:_buildPaths()
	local queue = self.buildQueue
	local taken = math.min(#queue, self.settings.buildBudget)
	if taken == 0 then
		return
	end
	for position = 1, taken do
		local index = queue[position]
		if self.state[index] == FLYING and not self.pathBuilt[index] then
			local start = self.path[index].segs[1]
			self.path[index] = Trajectory.build(start.p0, start.v0, start.rot0, start.w, self.pieces[index].halfExt, 1,
				self.gravity[index], self.bounciness[index], self.friction[index], self.castRay, self.pathRules)
			self.pathBuilt[index] = true
		end
	end
	local remaining = {}
	for position = taken + 1, #queue do
		table.insert(remaining, queue[position])
	end
	self.buildQueue = remaining
end

-- The poses of this frame are gathered in the move lists (flying pieces, then driven ones) and
-- handed to the display in one go. The lists are cut to `count`: a display may pass
-- them straight to BulkMoveTo.
function Play:_flush(count)
	local indices = self.moveIndices
	local frames = self.moveFrames
	for position = count + 1, self.moveCount do
		indices[position] = nil
		frames[position] = nil
	end
	self.moveCount = count
	if count > 0 then
		self.display.move(indices, frames, count)
	end
end

-- Returns how many poses it put in the move lists.
function Play:_moveFlying()
	local flying = self.flying
	local count = 0
	local position = 1
	while position <= #flying do
		local index = flying[position]
		-- A piece a Continuous Force took over is dropped from the list here.
		if self.state[index] ~= FLYING then
			local last = #flying
			flying[position] = flying[last]
			flying[last] = nil
			continue
		end
		local path = self.path[index]
		local elapsed = self.clock - self.pathStart[index]
		-- A lost piece leaves before it is listed: the display moves every piece it is handed,
		-- and one whose stand-in is gone stops the whole move (Reactor/Display.move).
		if self.pathBuilt[index] and path.restT == math.huge and elapsed > self.airTime then
			local last = #flying
			flying[position] = flying[last]
			flying[last] = nil
			self.state[index] = GONE
			self.display.drop(index)
			self.awake -= 1
			continue
		end
		local frame = Trajectory.evaluate(path, elapsed, self.gravity[index])
		self.lastFrame[index] = frame
		count += 1
		self.moveIndices[count] = index
		self.moveFrames[count] = frame

		if self.pathBuilt[index] and elapsed >= path.restT then
			local last = #flying
			flying[position] = flying[last]
			flying[last] = nil
			self.state[index] = LANDED
			self.landedAfter[index] = path.restT
		else
			position += 1
		end
	end
	return count
end

function Play:step(dt)
	self.clock += dt
	if self.phase == "fading" then
		return After.fade(self, dt)
	elseif self.phase == "returning" then
		return After.back(self, dt)
	elseif self.phase == "closing" then
		return After.close(self, dt)
	end

	self:_followForces()
	self:_wakePending()
	if self.supportStale then
		self:_collapse()
	end
	self:_buildPaths()
	self:_flush(Crack.settle(self, Driven.step(self, dt, self:_moveFlying())))

	if #self.flying > 0 or #self.driven > 0 or #self.pendingWake > 0 or #self.pendingCrack > 0 or next(self.kicks) ~= nil then
		self.idleFor = 0
		return "active"
	end
	if self.hidden == 0 then
		return "done"
	end
	local after = self.settings.After
	-- Something to fade or to bring back: what has landed and, for a Return, what is cracked.
	local settles = self.awake > 0 and After.anyLanded(self)
	if after == "Return" and next(self.crackFrame) ~= nil then
		settles = true
	end
	-- A wound gives its ground back whatever was moved in it (After.close).
	if self.settings.closes then
		settles = true
	end
	if after == "Stay" or not settles then
		return "dormant"
	end
	self.idleFor += dt
	if self.idleFor >= self.settings.AfterDelay then
		self.phaseTime = 0
		self.phase = After.begin(self)
	end
	return "active"
end

-- Stands the whole Reactor up as stand-ins, the originals hidden: for a play whose rest poses
-- are somewhere other than the parts (Reactor/Pieces.carry). Nothing is let go: a piece stays
-- where it stands until a Force pushes it or it loses its support. Called once, on a new play.
function Play:place()
	if self.placed then
		return
	end
	self.placed = true
	for index in ipairs(self.pieces) do
		self.display.wake(index)
		self.awake += 1
		self.hidden += 1
	end
end

-- Everything back: stand-ins removed, originals shown, the play as new. A piece that was cut
-- again stays out of it: its pieces stand for it.
function Play:restore()
	for index, piece in ipairs(self.pieces) do
		if self.state[index] ~= RESTING or self.placed or self.crackFrame[index] then
			self.display.restore(index)
			self.state[index] = RESTING
			if piece.retired then
				self.state[index] = GONE
			end
		end
	end
	self.placed = false
	self.flying = {}
	self.driven = {}
	self.track = {}
	self.pendingWake = {}
	self.pendingPush = {}
	self.cracked = {}
	self.crackFrame = {}
	self.pendingCrack = {}
	self.buildQueue = {}
	self.kicks = {}
	self:_flush(0)
	self.awake = 0
	self.hidden = 0
	self.phase = "live"
	self.phaseTime = 0
	self.idleFor = 0
end

Play.RESTING = RESTING
Play.FLYING = FLYING
Play.LANDED = LANDED
Play.GONE = GONE
Play.DRIVEN = DRIVEN

return Play

--[[
	Recrack  -  the later cracks of one Reactor's play, taken one after another.

	Reactor/init asks for one each time an Impulse reaches a Reactor that is out of place
	already (Recrack.request). Reactor/Recut plans it, Reactor/Shards cuts the pieces, which
	takes a few frames, Recut puts them into the play, and the Force that asked is then given
	to the new pieces late (Play:kickAgain), as a Reactor's first cut answers its Force late.
	A second request waits for the first: it is planned on the pieces the first one left.

	One Force cracks one place once: asked again where it last cracked, it is given nothing
	(Reactor/Entries asks for every Force a Reactor is told of, and is told again of one that
	has moved). Another Force at that place cracks the ground again: its rings are laid from
	other numbers, so the pieces that stand there are cut finer and moved on.

	Recrack.request(entry, record, kicked, isCurrent, revive)
	    entry: Reactor/init's, with play, pieceCount (the Reactor's Pieces) and cracks (the
	    requests waiting, oldest first); a wound of Reactor/Wounds has that shape. Recrack keeps
	    two fields of its own on it: places (record -> where it last cracked) and taken (the
	    cracks planned so far). kicked: the record's own list of the pieces it has
	    kicked in this play (Play.kicks[record], or what Play:strike returned for an Impulse that
	    is over); nil asks for nothing. isCurrent() -> whether the entry is still its Reactor's:
	    a Reactor put back while a cut runs gets nothing. revive(): the play has work again.
	Recrack.opened(entry, records, hit)
	    The entry's first cut was made around `hit`: the first Impulse of `records` that stands
	    there has cracked that place, and asks for nothing more at it.
]]

local Recut = require(script.Parent.Recut)
local Shards = require(script.Parent.Shards)
local Sites = require(script.Parent.Sites)

-- A Force within this many studs of where it last cracked is at that place still.
local SAME_PLACE = 1
-- Keeps the rings of one crack apart from those of the crack before it at the same place.
local SEED_STEP = 104729

local Recrack = {}

-- record -> where it last cracked this entry's ground; a record that is over is forgotten.
local function placesOf(entry)
	if not entry.places then
		entry.places = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })
	end
	return entry.places
end

local function takeNext(entry, isCurrent, revive)
	local request = entry.cracks[1]
	if not request then
		return
	end
	local play = entry.play
	local record = request.record

	-- The Force left the standing crust alone while its crack was cut (Play.recracking): it
	-- kicks now, the new pieces and those that joined (`indices`) included.
	local function finish(indices)
		table.remove(entry.cracks, 1)
		play.recracking[record] = nil
		play:kickAgain(record, request.kicked, indices or {})
		revive()
		takeNext(entry, isCurrent, revive)
	end

	if play.phase ~= "live" then
		finish(nil)
		return
	end
	local hit = record.field.origin.Position
	-- A Force may name the pieces of its own crack (record.pieces, Force/Registry).
	entry.taken = (entry.taken or 0) + 1
	local seed = Sites.seedAt(hit) + entry.taken * SEED_STEP
	local plan = Recut.plan(play, hit, record.field.range, record.pieces or entry.pieceCount, seed)
	if not plan then
		finish(nil)
		return
	end
	if #plan.jobs == 0 then
		finish(Recut.apply(play, plan, {}))
		return
	end
	Shards.recut(plan.jobs, function(results)
		if not isCurrent() then
			table.clear(entry.cracks)
			return
		end
		if play.phase ~= "live" then
			finish(nil)
			return
		end
		finish(Recut.apply(play, plan, results))
	end)
end

function Recrack.request(entry, record, kicked, isCurrent, revive)
	if not kicked then
		return
	end
	local places = placesOf(entry)
	local hit = record.field.origin.Position
	local last = places[record]
	if last and (last - hit).Magnitude < SAME_PLACE then
		return
	end
	places[record] = hit
	table.insert(entry.cracks, { record = record, kicked = kicked })
	entry.play.recracking[record] = true
	if #entry.cracks == 1 then
		takeNext(entry, isCurrent, revive)
	end
end

function Recrack.opened(entry, records, hit)
	for _, record in ipairs(records) do
		local stands = record.field.origin.Position
		if record.actsAs == "Impulse" and (stands - hit).Magnitude < SAME_PLACE then
			placesOf(entry)[record] = stands
			return
		end
	end
end

return Recrack

--[[
	Recut  -  a later crack in ground that is cracked already (Shard Pattern "Cracks"). Part of
	Reactor/Play, split out for size: the functions that take a play read and write its own
	tables. Maths on Vector3 and CFrame values; the engine's cut itself is Reactor/Shards.recut.

	A part keeps its first cut for as long as its play lasts. A later Impulse on the same face
	gets rings of its own (Reactor/Sites.cracks around its own hit), at the place of an earlier
	hit as anywhere else: that place is then cracked finer and deeper. Every crust piece that
	still stands and that two or more of those points fall in is cut again around them: it
	leaves the play, its pieces take its place and carry a strike of their own, so the crater,
	the rim and the hairlines are measured from the new hit. A standing piece within the new
	reach that is not cut joins the new crack as it is. Pieces already thrown are left alone,
	and so is the base.

	Cracks pile up: a piece keeps what earlier cracks did to it, and the new crack moves it on
	from where it stands (Reactor/Crack.pose), so the new crater, rim and hairlines all show.

	A crack is never refused for want of room in the play's Max Pieces: its pieces are then cut
	around fewer points, the ones nearest the hit first, and a piece with no room at all joins
	the crack whole.

	Which piece a point falls in is the engine's own rule: the nearest point of a cut owns the
	space. A piece of a part's first cut carries that cut's points (sites) and its own place
	among them (siteIndex). A piece that was cut again carries the points of that cut
	(cutPoints) and the pieces it gave, by their place among those points (children).

	Recut.plan(play, hit, reach, count, seed) -> plan or nil
	    hit: where the Force is, in the world. reach: its Range. count: the points a part is
	    cut around (the Reactor's Pieces). seed: the rings' numbers; Reactor/Recrack gives
	    every crack its own, or a second hit at one place would lay the first one's points
	    again and cut nothing. nil when nothing standing is within the rings.
	    plan.jobs: { { index, template, points, strike, within }, ... }: each piece to cut, the
	    fragment it is drawn from, and the points in the part's own space. within: the piece
	    lies inside the new reach, so it joins the new crack whole if the engine refuses the cut.
	    plan.joins: { { index, strike }, ... }: the pieces that join the new crack uncut.
	Recut.apply(play, plan, results) -> indices
	    results[position]: the shards the engine gave for plan.jobs[position] (Reactor/Shards),
	    or false. Returns every piece the new crack made or took over: the Force that made it
	    has passed them by, and Play:kickAgain gives them its kick.
]]

local Sites = require(script.Parent.Sites)
local Pieces = require(script.Parent.Pieces)

local RESTING = 0
local GONE = 3

-- Two unit normals with at least this dot product face the same way.
local SAME_FACE = 0.99
-- A piece whose longest edge is under this many studs is not cut again.
local LEAST_RECUT = 1.5

local Recut = {}

-- Where a piece's part stands for the play: where it is, or where the Reactor was stood up.
local function partFrame(piece)
	return piece.rest * piece.box:Inverse()
end

local function stands(play, index)
	local piece = play.pieces[index]
	return play.state[index] == RESTING and play.pendingPush[index] == nil and not piece.retired and not piece.fixed
end

-- The place in `points` of the one nearest to `point`.
local function nearest(points, point)
	local best = nil
	local least = math.huge
	for index, candidate in ipairs(points) do
		local distance = (candidate - point).Magnitude
		if distance < least then
			least = distance
			best = index
		end
	end
	return best
end

-- The piece of a part's crust a point of the part's space falls in today, or nil where the
-- first cut gave no piece. Walks from the first cut down through every later one.
local function ownerOf(play, ground, point)
	local index = ground.pieceOf[nearest(ground.sites, point)]
	while index do
		local piece = play.pieces[index]
		if not piece.retired then
			return index
		end
		index = piece.children[nearest(piece.cutPoints, point)]
	end
	return nil
end

-- Every cracked ground of the play: its frame, its size, its first cut and its strikes. A
-- ground is a part, or one patch of a part (piece.cut, Reactor/Pieces.ofSet): the space one
-- first cut was made in.
local function grounds(play)
	local bySpace = {}
	local ordered = {}
	local live = 0
	for index, piece in ipairs(play.pieces) do
		if not piece.retired then
			live += 1
		end
		if piece.box and piece.siteIndex and not piece.fixed then
			local space = piece.cut or piece.part
			local ground = bySpace[space]
			if not ground then
				local size = piece.part.Size
				if piece.cut then
					size = piece.cut.size
				end
				ground = { size = size, face = piece.cut and piece.cut.face, frame = partFrame(piece), pieceOf = {}, strikes = {}, pieces = {} }
				bySpace[space] = ground
				table.insert(ordered, ground)
			end
			table.insert(ground.pieces, index)
			if piece.sites then
				ground.sites = piece.sites
				ground.pieceOf[piece.siteIndex] = index
			end
			if piece.strike and not table.find(ground.strikes, piece.strike) then
				table.insert(ground.strikes, piece.strike)
			end
		end
	end
	return ordered, live
end

-- The new crack of one part: its jobs and joins are added to the plan. Returns how many
-- pieces the cuts would add.
local function planGround(play, ground, hit, reach, count, random, plan)
	if not ground.sites or #ground.strikes == 0 then
		return 0
	end
	local frame = ground.frame
	local size = ground.size
	local hitInPart = frame:PointToObjectSpace(hit)
	local points = Sites.count(size, count)
	if points < 2 or (hitInPart - Sites.hitIn(size, hitInPart)).Magnitude > reach * Sites.RUN_ON then
		return 0
	end
	local offsets, cut = Sites.cracks(size, points, hitInPart, reach, random, ground.face)
	local first = ground.strikes[1]
	local normal = frame:VectorToObjectSpace(first.normal)
	if cut.normal:Dot(normal) < SAME_FACE then
		return 0
	end
	local origin = frame:PointToWorldSpace(cut.origin)
	-- The crust keeps the thickness of the part's first cut, and the new points lie at its middle.
	local strike = { origin = origin, normal = first.normal, reach = cut.reach, crust = first.crust }
	local shift = normal * ((cut.crust - first.crust) / 2)

	local byPiece = {}
	for _, offset in ipairs(offsets) do
		local point = offset + shift
		local owner = ownerOf(play, ground, point)
		if owner and stands(play, owner) then
			local list = byPiece[owner]
			if not list then
				list = {}
				byPiece[owner] = list
			end
			table.insert(list, point)
		end
	end

	local added = 0
	for _, index in ipairs(ground.pieces) do
		if stands(play, index) then
			local piece = play.pieces[index]
			local offset = piece.rest.Position - origin
			local flat = offset - first.normal * offset:Dot(first.normal)
			local within = flat.Magnitude <= strike.reach
			local list = byPiece[index]
			if list and #list >= 2 and piece.reach >= LEAST_RECUT then
				table.insert(plan.jobs, { index = index, template = piece.shard, points = list, strike = strike, within = within })
				added += #list - 1
			elseif within then
				table.insert(plan.joins, { index = index, strike = strike })
			end
		end
	end
	return added
end

-- Holds a plan to the room the budget has left. Reactor/Sites.cracks lays its points from
-- the hit outward, so the ones dropped are the farthest.
local function fit(plan, room)
	local jobs = {}
	for _, job in ipairs(plan.jobs) do
		local points = job.points
		for position = #points, math.max(room + 2, 1), -1 do
			points[position] = nil
		end
		if #points >= 2 then
			room -= #points - 1
			table.insert(jobs, job)
		elseif job.within then
			table.insert(plan.joins, { index = job.index, strike = job.strike })
		end
	end
	plan.jobs = jobs
end

function Recut.plan(play, hit, reach, count, seed)
	local ordered, live = grounds(play)
	local plan = { jobs = {}, joins = {} }
	for position, ground in ipairs(ordered) do
		planGround(play, ground, hit, reach, count, Sites.sequence(seed + position * 7919), plan)
	end
	if #plan.jobs == 0 and #plan.joins == 0 then
		return nil
	end
	fit(plan, play.settings.MaxPieces - live)
	return plan
end

-- Takes one cut piece out of the play and puts its pieces in. Mutates the play's own tables.
-- A piece that was stood out of place hands that place on: its pieces stand where it stood
-- until the new crack moves them. The new pieces are added to `taken`, and those that stand
-- out of place to the two move lists.
local function replace(play, job, shards, taken, movedIndices, movedFrames)
	local leaf = play.pieces[job.index]
	local siblings = leaf.siblings
	local place = table.find(siblings, job.index)
	if place then
		table.remove(siblings, place)
	end
	local stood = play.crackFrame[job.index]
	local children = {}
	local shown = nil
	for _, shard in ipairs(shards) do
		local rest = leaf.rest * leaf.box:ToObjectSpace(shard.box)
		local piece = Pieces.ofShard(leaf.part, rest, shard)
		piece.siblings = siblings
		piece.strike = job.strike
		piece.cut = leaf.cut
		if leaf.cut and Pieces.touchesSide(shard.box, piece.halfExt, leaf.cut) then
			piece.atEdge = true
		end
		table.insert(play.pieces, piece)
		local index = #play.pieces
		play.state[index] = RESTING
		table.insert(siblings, index)
		table.insert(taken, index)
		if shard.siteIndex then
			children[shard.siteIndex] = index
		end
		shown = shown or index
		if stood then
			local frame = stood * leaf.rest:ToObjectSpace(rest)
			play.crackFrame[index] = frame
			table.insert(movedIndices, index)
			table.insert(movedFrames, frame)
		end
	end
	leaf.retired = true
	leaf.children = children
	leaf.cutPoints = job.points
	play.state[job.index] = GONE
	play.cracked[job.index] = nil
	play.crackFrame[job.index] = nil
	play.display.drop(job.index)
	-- The part is hidden for as long as its cut pieces stand in for it: that counts once.
	if not stood then
		play.hidden += 1
	end
	-- Waking one piece shows every piece of its part that has no stand-in yet (Reactor/Display).
	play.display.wake(shown)
end

function Recut.apply(play, plan, results)
	local taken = {}
	local movedIndices = {}
	local movedFrames = {}
	local function join(index, strike)
		if not stands(play, index) then
			return
		end
		local piece = play.pieces[index]
		piece.strike = strike
		play.cracked[index] = nil
		table.insert(taken, index)
	end
	for position, job in ipairs(plan.jobs) do
		local shards = results[position]
		if shards and #shards >= 2 and stands(play, job.index) then
			replace(play, job, shards, taken, movedIndices, movedFrames)
		elseif job.within then
			join(job.index, job.strike)
		end
	end
	for _, joined in ipairs(plan.joins) do
		join(joined.index, joined.strike)
	end
	if #movedIndices > 0 then
		play.display.move(movedIndices, movedFrames, #movedIndices)
	end
	-- Reactor/Support's graph names pieces by their place in the list, which has grown.
	play.support = nil
	return taken
end

return Recut

--[[
	Shards  -  what a part breaks into with Break = "Shards": real fragments, cut by the engine
	(GeometryService:FragmentAsync) around points of ours (Reactor/Sites) and kept OUT of the
	world as templates. Reactor/Display copies its stand-ins from them; the part itself is read
	and never changed. Break = "Blocks" comes here as well for a part that is not a plain box:
	cut around an even grid of points (Reactor/Dice.centres), its fragments are cubes.

	The cut yields (about 30 ms for 50 shards of a plain part, measured in Studio), and a play
	needs its pieces up front. So shards are cut ahead and kept per part under a key that names
	everything the cut depends on; Reactor/init asks for them and, when they are not there yet,
	has them cut and lets the Reactor answer its Force a few frames late.

	Shards.cuttable(part) -> boolean      a Part, wedge, MeshPart or union that draws its own
	                                      shape; a Part carrying a mesh, a truss and Terrain are not
	Shards.key(part, count, seed, hit, reach, grid) -> string
	Shards.get(part, key) -> shards | false | nil
	    shards: { { template, box, size, standOffset, fixed, siteIndex }, ... }
	        template     the fragment, a MeshPart with no parent
	        box          the shard's own box as a frame in the PART's space; size its extents
	        standOffset  where the template sits in that box's frame: a stand-in at frame F of
	                     the piece has CFrame F * standOffset
	        fixed        true for the base under cracked ground: it never moves
	        siteIndex    the place, among the points of its cut, of the point it was cut around
	    shards.sites     the points of the cut, in the part's space
	    shards.strike    for cracked ground, Sites.cracks' strike, in the part's space
	    Cracked ground is cut twice: the part into its crust and its base (two points, a flat
	    face between), then the crust alone into its pieces. The base is one shard.
	    false: the engine refused the part, or gave fewer than two shards; it moves whole.
	    nil: not cut under that key yet.
	Shards.prepare(jobs, done)
	    jobs: { { part, key, count, seed, hit, reach, grid, face, loose }, ... }. Cuts them, a few at a time,
	    and calls done() once all are kept. Returns at once. No hit: Sites.even. A hit (a point of
	    the part's box): Sites.aroundHit. A hit and a reach: Sites.cracks, the hit as it is.
	    grid = true: Dice.centres, for blocks. face: the face Sites.cracks is to crack.
	    loose = true: the part is a template kept out of the world (Reactor/Patches), which
	    whoever asked must hold on to until done() has read its set.
	Shards.recut(jobs, done)
	    jobs: { { template, points }, ... } (Reactor/Recut's): cuts each template, a fragment of an
	    earlier cut, around its points, which are in the space of the part it came from. Calls
	    done(results) with the shards of each job, or false, in the jobs' order. Returns at once.
	    These are a play's own and are not kept.

	Kept sets are held by the part alone (weak keys): they go when the part does, and a part
	cut again under another key drops its old set. Nothing here is saved with the place: the
	engine does not keep fragments across sessions, so they are cut again in each.
]]

local GeometryService = game:GetService("GeometryService")
local Sites = require(script.Parent.Sites)
local Dice = require(script.Parent.Dice)

-- Cuts running at once.
local WORKERS = 4
-- A hit is the same hit within this many studs: the key rounds to it.
local HIT_STEP = 0.5

local Shards = {}

-- part -> { key = string, shards = table or false }
local kept = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })

function Shards.cuttable(part)
	if part:IsA("MeshPart") or part:IsA("PartOperation") then
		return true
	end
	if part:IsA("Part") or part:IsA("WedgePart") or part:IsA("CornerWedgePart") then
		-- A Part that carries a mesh draws the mesh, which is not what the engine would cut.
		return part:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("DataModelMesh") == nil
	end
	return false
end

function Shards.key(part, count, seed, hit, reach, grid)
	local size = part.Size
	local shape = part.ClassName
	if part:IsA("MeshPart") then
		shape ..= part.MeshId
	elseif part:IsA("Part") then
		shape ..= part.Shape.Name
	end
	local where = "even"
	if hit then
		where = string.format("%d,%d,%d", math.round(hit.X / HIT_STEP), math.round(hit.Y / HIT_STEP), math.round(hit.Z / HIT_STEP))
	end
	if reach then
		where = string.format("cracks:%s:%d", where, math.round(reach / HIT_STEP))
	end
	if grid then
		where = "blocks"
	end
	return string.format("%s|%.3f,%.3f,%.3f|%d|%d|%s", shape, size.X, size.Y, size.Z, count, seed, where)
end

function Shards.get(part, key)
	local set = kept[part]
	if set and set.key == key then
		return set.shards
	end
	return nil
end

-- The engine's fragments of `part` around world points, or nil. Yields. A wedge is refused as
-- it is and accepted as a union of itself alone.
local function fragment(part, points)
	local ok, result = pcall(function()
		return GeometryService:FragmentAsync(part, points)
	end)
	if ok and type(result) == "table" then
		return result
	end
	local united, union = pcall(function()
		return GeometryService:UnionAsync(part, {})
	end)
	local solid = united and type(union) == "table" and union[1] or nil
	if not solid then
		return nil
	end
	ok, result = pcall(function()
		return GeometryService:FragmentAsync(solid, points)
	end)
	solid:Destroy()
	if ok and type(result) == "table" then
		return result
	end
	return nil
end

-- A fragment as a shard of the part whose frame is `frame`.
local function shardOf(template, frame, fixed, siteIndex)
	local extents = template.ExtentsCFrame
	return {
		template = template,
		box = frame:ToObjectSpace(extents),
		size = template.ExtentsSize,
		standOffset = extents:ToObjectSpace(template.CFrame),
		fixed = fixed,
		siteIndex = siteIndex,
	}
end

-- Cuts one job and returns its shards, or false. Yields.
local function cut(job)
	local part = job.part
	if not part.Parent and not job.loose then
		return false
	end
	local frame = part.CFrame
	local random = Sites.sequence(job.seed)
	local offsets
	local strike, split = nil, nil
	if job.grid then
		offsets = Dice.centres(part.Size, job.count)
	elseif job.reach then
		-- A ground's patch (loose) is always cut: one left whole could never crack again.
		offsets, strike, split = Sites.cracks(part.Size, job.count, job.hit, job.reach, random, job.face, job.loose == true)
	elseif job.hit then
		offsets = Sites.aroundHit(part.Size, job.count, job.hit, random)
	else
		offsets = Sites.even(part.Size, job.count, random)
	end
	local points = table.create(#offsets)
	for index, offset in ipairs(offsets) do
		points[index] = frame:PointToWorldSpace(offset)
	end

	-- Cracked ground: the crust is cut off its base first, and only the crust into pieces.
	-- A fragment's Index is the place of its point among those the cut was given.
	local source = part
	local crust, base = nil, nil
	if split then
		local halves = fragment(part, { frame:PointToWorldSpace(split.inCrust), frame:PointToWorldSpace(split.inBase) })
		if halves and #halves == 2 then
			for _, entry in ipairs(halves) do
				if entry.Index == 1 then
					crust = entry.Instance
				else
					base = entry.Instance
				end
			end
		end
		if crust and base then
			source = crust
		else
			base = nil
		end
	end

	local fragments = fragment(source, points)
	if crust then
		crust:Destroy()
	end
	if not fragments or #fragments < 2 then
		if base then
			base:Destroy()
		end
		return false
	end
	local shards = table.create(#fragments + 1)
	for _, entry in ipairs(fragments) do
		table.insert(shards, shardOf(entry.Instance, frame, false, entry.Index))
	end
	if base then
		table.insert(shards, shardOf(base, frame, true, nil))
	end
	shards.sites = offsets
	shards.strike = strike
	return shards
end

-- Cuts one fragment of an earlier cut again and returns its shards, or false. Yields. A
-- fragment keeps the frame of the part it was cut from, which is the frame its points are in.
local function cutAgain(job)
	local template = job.template
	local frame = template.CFrame
	local points = table.create(#job.points)
	for index, offset in ipairs(job.points) do
		points[index] = frame:PointToWorldSpace(offset)
	end
	local fragments = fragment(template, points)
	if not fragments or #fragments < 2 then
		return false
	end
	local shards = table.create(#fragments)
	for _, entry in ipairs(fragments) do
		table.insert(shards, shardOf(entry.Instance, frame, false, entry.Index))
	end
	return shards
end

function Shards.prepare(jobs, done)
	local total = #jobs
	if total == 0 then
		done()
		return
	end
	local taken = 0
	local finished = 0
	local function work()
		while taken < total do
			taken += 1
			local job = jobs[taken]
			local ok, shards = pcall(cut, job)
			kept[job.part] = { key = job.key, shards = ok and shards or false }
			finished += 1
		end
		if finished == total and done then
			local callback = done
			done = nil
			callback()
		end
	end
	for _ = 1, math.min(WORKERS, total) do
		task.spawn(work)
	end
end

function Shards.recut(jobs, done)
	local total = #jobs
	local results = table.create(total, false)
	if total == 0 then
		done(results)
		return
	end
	local taken = 0
	local finished = 0
	local function work()
		while taken < total do
			taken += 1
			local position = taken
			local ok, shards = pcall(cutAgain, jobs[position])
			results[position] = ok and shards or false
			finished += 1
		end
		if finished == total and done then
			local callback = done
			done = nil
			callback(results)
		end
	end
	for _ = 1, math.min(WORKERS, total) do
		task.spawn(work)
	end
end

return Shards

--[[
	Sites  -  the points a part is broken around with Break = "Shards". The engine cuts one shard
	per point: the part of the solid that is nearer to that point than to any other (a Voronoi
	cell). So the number of points is the number of shards, and where the points are thick the
	shards are small. Numbers only, no instances.

	Sites.count(size, pieces) -> how many points a part of `size` gets
	    `pieces` held to Sites.MAX, and to fewer for a part too small to give that many shards
	    of LEAST_VOLUME each. Under 2 the part is not cut.
	Sites.even(size, count, random) -> { Vector3 }
	    anywhere in the part's box: shards of about one size.
	Sites.aroundHit(size, count, hit, random) -> { Vector3 }
	    NEAR_SHARE of the points near `hit`, the rest anywhere: small shards where the part was
	    struck, large ones away from it.
	Sites.hitIn(size, point) -> the point of the part's box nearest to `point`
	Sites.face(size, point) -> axis ("X" | "Y" | "Z"), side (1 | -1)
	    the face of the part's box that lies nearest to `point`: the one a Force there strikes.
	    Of faces about as near, the largest: a slab struck beside its edge cracks in its top.
	Sites.faceAxes(axis) -> the two axes a face normal to `axis` lies in: its u and its v
	Sites.underFace(size, axis, side, u, v, depth) -> the point of the part at (u, v) of a face,
	    `depth` under it
	Sites.alongFace(axis, u, v, normal) -> the vector with `u` and `v` along the face's two axes
	    and `normal` along `axis`
	Sites.probes(size, axis, side, u, v, reach) -> { Vector3 }: places just under a face, at
	    (u, v) and on three rings around it out to `reach`, to ask a Force's field at
	Sites.cracks(size, count, hit, reach, random, face, fill) -> { Vector3 }, strike, split
	    cracked ground: the points of a crust under the struck face, in rings around the hit
	    (rubble at the hit, cracks running out from it that fork, long pieces past the reach).
	    strike = { origin, normal, reach, crust }: the hit laid onto the struck face, that face's
	    outward normal, how far the rings go (`reach`, drawn in when the face is smaller) and
	    how thick the crust is.
	    split = { inCrust, inBase }: two points, one over the other; cut around them alone, the
	    part falls into the crust and the base under it, with a flat face between. The other
	    points are then for the crust only. nil for a part too thin for both: it is cut straight
	    through, and its crust is all of it.
	    `hit` may lie outside the part: a part beside the one struck gets the outer rings.
	    face = { axis, side } names the face to crack; without it, Sites.face(size, hit). A
	    patch of a ground (Reactor/Wounds) names its ground's face: a narrow patch of a thick
	    ground has a side larger than its top.
	    fill: the face is cut whatever the rings give it. A patch beside the hit that gets fewer
	    than two of their points has `count` points, two at least, spread over it. Reactor/Shards
	    asks it for a ground's patches; Reactor/Recut never does, since a later crack cuts only
	    where its rings fall.
	Sites.RUN_ON: how many times the reach the outermost cracks run to; a part farther from
	    the hit than that gets none of them.
	Sites.sequence(seed) -> random: numbers from 0 to 1, the same for the same seed
	Sites.seedAt(point) -> a seed that is the same for the same place: a Force emitted again
	    where it was cuts ground that is whole as it did (a later crack of ground that is
	    cracked adds a step of its own, Reactor/Recrack)
	Points and `hit` are offsets in the part's own space; points keep a little inside the box.
	`random` gives 0 to 1; the same sequence gives the same points. A point that falls outside
	the solid itself (the corner of a ball's box) cuts no shard, so a round part gives a few
	fewer than asked.
]]

local Sites = {}

Sites.MAX = 240
-- The average shard is never smaller than this, in cubic studs: a half-stud cube.
local LEAST_VOLUME = 0.125
-- Points stay within this share of the box, clear of its faces.
local INSET = 0.95
-- aroundHit: the share of the points gathered near the hit, how far from it they reach as a
-- share of the part's longest edge, and how strongly they crowd toward it (under 1 crowds).
local NEAR_SHARE = 0.7
local NEAR_REACH = 0.4
local CROWDING = 0.6

local AXES = { "X", "Y", "Z" }
local SIDES = { 1, -1 }
-- face: a face this much farther off than the nearest still counts as near as it.
local FACE_SLACK = 0.25
-- cracks: the share of the crust's points that is rubble right at the hit, and how far out it
-- lies (share of the reach).
local RUBBLE_SHARE = 0.1
local RUBBLE_REACH = 0.12
-- Bands crowd toward the hit: band i of n ends at (i / n) ^ BAND_CROWDING of the reach.
local BAND_CROWDING = 1.3
-- A crack forks where its piece would be this many times wider than deep.
local FORK_AT = 2.4
-- How unevenly the cracks leave the hit (share of their even spacing), and how far a piece's
-- point strays across its band (share of the band's depth).
local UNEVEN = 0.3
local ACROSS = 0.3
-- Past the reach the cracks run on as long pieces, to this many times the reach.
local RUN_ON = 1.9
Sites.RUN_ON = RUN_ON
local MOST_BANDS = 14
-- The crust is this share of the reach thick, never under LEAST_CRUST studs nor over
-- CRUST_SHARE of the part; a part that leaves no room for that has no base.
local CRUST_REACH_SHARE = 0.075
local LEAST_CRUST = 0.5
local CRUST_SHARE = 0.45

function Sites.sequence(seed)
	local state = seed % 2147483647
	return function()
		state = (state * 48271 + 11) % 2147483647
		return state / 2147483647
	end
end

function Sites.seedAt(point)
	return math.floor(math.abs(point.X * 31.7 + point.Y * 57.3 + point.Z * 17.1) * 1000) % 2147483646 + 1
end

function Sites.count(size, pieces)
	local wanted = math.floor(math.min(pieces, Sites.MAX))
	local room = math.floor(size.X * size.Y * size.Z / LEAST_VOLUME)
	return math.max(math.min(wanted, room), 0)
end

local function anywhere(size, random)
	return Vector3.new((random() - 0.5) * size.X, (random() - 0.5) * size.Y, (random() - 0.5) * size.Z) * INSET
end

function Sites.even(size, count, random)
	local points = table.create(count)
	for index = 1, count do
		points[index] = anywhere(size, random)
	end
	return points
end

function Sites.hitIn(size, point)
	local half = size / 2
	return Vector3.new(math.clamp(point.X, -half.X, half.X), math.clamp(point.Y, -half.Y, half.Y), math.clamp(point.Z, -half.Z, half.Z))
end

function Sites.aroundHit(size, count, hit, random)
	local points = table.create(count)
	local reach = math.max(size.X, size.Y, size.Z) * NEAR_REACH
	local near = math.floor(count * NEAR_SHARE)
	for index = 1, count do
		if index > near then
			points[index] = anywhere(size, random)
		else
			local direction = Vector3.new(random() - 0.5, random() - 0.5, random() - 0.5)
			if direction.Magnitude < 1e-4 then
				direction = Vector3.new(0, 1, 0)
			end
			local offset = hit + direction.Unit * (reach * random() ^ CROWDING)
			points[index] = Sites.hitIn(size, offset) * INSET
		end
	end
	return points
end

-- How far `point` lies from the face of the box across `axis` on `side`, as a rectangle.
local function faceDistance(size, point, axis, side)
	local squared = (point[axis] - side * size[axis] / 2) ^ 2
	for _, other in ipairs(AXES) do
		if other ~= axis then
			local past = math.max(math.abs(point[other]) - size[other] / 2, 0)
			squared += past * past
		end
	end
	return math.sqrt(squared)
end

function Sites.face(size, point)
	local bestAxis, bestSide = "Y", 1
	local least, bestArea = math.huge, 0
	for _, axis in ipairs(AXES) do
		local area = size.X * size.Y * size.Z / size[axis]
		for _, side in ipairs(SIDES) do
			local distance = faceDistance(size, point, axis, side)
			local clearlyNearer = distance < least * (1 - FACE_SLACK)
			local asNearAndLarger = distance <= least * (1 + FACE_SLACK) and area > bestArea
			if clearlyNearer or asNearAndLarger then
				bestAxis, bestSide = axis, side
				least, bestArea = distance, area
			end
		end
	end
	return bestAxis, bestSide
end

-- The two axes a face normal to `axis` lies in.
local function faceAxes(axis)
	if axis == "X" then
		return "Y", "Z"
	elseif axis == "Y" then
		return "X", "Z"
	end
	return "X", "Y"
end

-- A point of the part from its place (u, v) in a face and its depth under that face.
local function underFace(size, axis, side, u, v, depth)
	local along = side * (size[axis] / 2 - depth)
	if axis == "X" then
		return Vector3.new(along, u, v)
	elseif axis == "Y" then
		return Vector3.new(u, along, v)
	end
	return Vector3.new(u, v, along)
end

-- The angle after `angle` in a ring of angles that goes once round.
local function nextIn(angles, index)
	local following = angles[index % #angles + 1]
	if following <= angles[index] then
		following += 2 * math.pi
	end
	return following
end

-- The ring's places (u, v) around (hitU, hitV), for `count` points. inside(u, v) keeps a place.
local function rings(count, hitU, hitV, reach, random, inside)
	local places = {}
	local function add(u, v)
		-- A place outside the part cuts nothing: it is left out, never pushed onto the edge.
		if inside(u, v) then
			table.insert(places, { u, v })
		end
	end

	local rubble = math.floor(count * RUBBLE_SHARE)
	for _ = 1, rubble do
		local angle = random() * 2 * math.pi
		local radius = reach * RUBBLE_REACH * math.sqrt(random())
		add(hitU + math.cos(angle) * radius, hitV + math.sin(angle) * radius)
	end

	-- More cracks leave the hit the more pieces there are to make.
	local cracksAtHit = math.clamp(math.round(math.sqrt(count) * 0.9), 6, 16) + math.floor(random() * 3)
	local angles = {}
	local turn = random() * 2 * math.pi
	for index = 1, cracksAtHit do
		angles[index] = turn + (index - 1 + (random() - 0.5) * 2 * UNEVEN) / cracksAtHit * 2 * math.pi
	end

	local function edges(band, bands)
		local inner = reach * (RUBBLE_REACH + (1 - RUBBLE_REACH) * ((band - 1) / bands) ^ BAND_CROWDING)
		local outer = reach * (RUBBLE_REACH + (1 - RUBBLE_REACH) * (band / bands) ^ BAND_CROWDING)
		return inner, outer
	end
	-- The points `bands` bands take, forks counted in, with the long pieces past the reach.
	local function cost(bands)
		local total = 0
		local across = cracksAtHit
		for band = 1, bands do
			local inner, outer = edges(band, bands)
			if math.pi * (inner + outer) / across > FORK_AT * (outer - inner) then
				across *= 2
			end
			total += across
		end
		return total + across
	end
	local bands = 1
	while bands < MOST_BANDS and cost(bands + 1) <= count - rubble do
		bands += 1
	end

	for band = 1, bands + 1 do
		local inner, outer = edges(math.min(band, bands), bands)
		if band > bands then
			inner = reach
			outer = reach * RUN_ON
		end
		local depth = outer - inner
		if band <= bands and math.pi * (inner + outer) / #angles > FORK_AT * depth then
			local forked = {}
			for index, angle in ipairs(angles) do
				table.insert(forked, angle)
				table.insert(forked, angle + (nextIn(angles, index) - angle) * (0.5 + (random() - 0.5) * 0.3))
			end
			angles = forked
		end
		for index, angle in ipairs(angles) do
			-- A piece's point sits midway between its two cracks.
			local along = (angle + nextIn(angles, index)) / 2
			local radius = (inner + outer) / 2 + (random() - 0.5) * 2 * ACROSS * depth
			add(hitU + math.cos(along) * radius, hitV + math.sin(along) * radius)
		end
	end
	return places
end

-- About `count` places (two or more asked) spread over a face of half-lengths halfU and halfV:
-- a grid of cells about as wide as they are long, each place off its cell's middle by up to
-- SPREAD_JITTER of the cell.
local SPREAD_JITTER = 0.25
local function spread(count, halfU, halfV, random)
	local columns = math.clamp(math.round(math.sqrt(count * halfU / halfV)), 1, count)
	local rows = math.max(math.round(count / columns), 1)
	local places = {}
	for row = 1, rows do
		for column = 1, columns do
			local u = (2 * (column - 0.5 + (random() - 0.5) * 2 * SPREAD_JITTER) / columns - 1) * halfU * INSET
			local v = (2 * (row - 0.5 + (random() - 0.5) * 2 * SPREAD_JITTER) / rows - 1) * halfV * INSET
			table.insert(places, { u, v })
		end
	end
	return places
end

Sites.faceAxes = faceAxes
Sites.underFace = underFace

function Sites.alongFace(axis, u, v, normal)
	if axis == "X" then
		return Vector3.new(normal, u, v)
	elseif axis == "Y" then
		return Vector3.new(u, normal, v)
	end
	return Vector3.new(u, v, normal)
end

-- How far under the face a probe lies.
local PROBE_DEPTH = 0.5

function Sites.probes(size, axis, side, u, v, reach)
	local points = { underFace(size, axis, side, u, v, PROBE_DEPTH) }
	for ring = 1, 3 do
		local radius = reach * ring * 0.3
		for step = 1, 8 do
			local angle = step / 8 * 2 * math.pi
			table.insert(points, underFace(size, axis, side, u + math.cos(angle) * radius, v + math.sin(angle) * radius, PROBE_DEPTH))
		end
	end
	return points
end

function Sites.cracks(size, count, hit, reach, random, face, fill)
	local axis, side = Sites.face(size, hit)
	if face then
		axis, side = face.axis, face.side
	end
	local uAxis, vAxis = faceAxes(axis)
	local halfU, halfV = size[uAxis] / 2, size[vAxis] / 2
	local hitU, hitV = hit[uAxis], hit[vAxis]
	local function inside(u, v)
		return math.abs(u) < halfU * INSET and math.abs(v) < halfV * INSET
	end

	-- The rings are drawn in to the face: none of the points is spent beyond its far corner.
	local farthest = math.sqrt((math.abs(hitU) + halfU) ^ 2 + (math.abs(hitV) + halfV) ^ 2)
	reach = math.min(reach, farthest / 1.2)

	local thickness = size[axis]
	local crust = math.min(math.max(reach * CRUST_REACH_SHARE, LEAST_CRUST), thickness * CRUST_SHARE)
	local split = nil
	if crust >= LEAST_CRUST then
		-- One point in the crust and one under it, in line: the cut between them is flat.
		local apart = math.min(crust, thickness - crust) / 2
		local u = math.clamp(hitU, -halfU * INSET, halfU * INSET)
		local v = math.clamp(hitV, -halfV * INSET, halfV * INSET)
		split = {
			inCrust = underFace(size, axis, side, u, v, crust - apart),
			inBase = underFace(size, axis, side, u, v, crust + apart),
		}
	else
		crust = thickness
	end

	-- Places that fall outside the part are lost (a hit near an edge loses many): the rings
	-- are drawn again for more, from the same numbers, until about as many are kept as asked.
	local seed = math.floor(random() * 2147483645) + 1
	local places = rings(count, hitU, hitV, reach, Sites.sequence(seed), inside)
	local asked = count
	for _ = 1, 16 do
		if #places >= count * 0.95 then
			break
		end
		asked = math.ceil(asked * 1.12)
		local more = rings(asked, hitU, hitV, reach, Sites.sequence(seed), inside)
		if #more > count then
			break
		end
		places = more
	end
	if fill and #places < 2 then
		places = spread(math.max(count, 2), halfU, halfV, Sites.sequence(seed))
	end
	local points = {}
	for _, place in ipairs(places) do
		table.insert(points, underFace(size, axis, side, place[1], place[2], crust / 2))
	end

	local strike = {
		origin = underFace(size, axis, side, hitU, hitV, 0),
		normal = underFace(Vector3.new(2, 2, 2), axis, side, 0, 0, 0),
		reach = reach,
		crust = crust,
	}
	return points, strike, split
end

return Sites
